title: Curie architecture atlas
subtitle: The production loop, its swappable seams, and the distance between current state and vision.

architectureGroups.label: Channel surface
architectureGroups.subtitle: 3 current · 1 planned
architectureGroups.description: One stable channel role in the architecture. Slack, Discord, and email are shipped implementations of this role; Teams remains planned. Concrete surfaces stay inside this expandable node.

architectureGroups.label: Sandbox substrate
architectureGroups.subtitle: 2 proven implementations
architectureGroups.description: The stable substrate role beneath sandbox lifecycle. Kubernetes and Docker prove that the same boundary has multiple implementations.

architectureGroups.label: Bot capabilities
architectureGroups.subtitle: 1 shipped example, 2 patterns
architectureGroups.description: Reasons to buy rather than architecture peers of the worker or the runner. Each one is a bundle, an eval set, and an operating pattern that rides the isolated runtime. Expand to see the individual capabilities.

architectureGroups.label: Deployed agent
architectureGroups.subtitle: Identity, bundle, deployment
architectureGroups.description: One agent as an install sees it. An agent may be authored elsewhere; what Curie adds is an identity, a bundle it can deploy, and a channel to answer on. Expand to see the three parts.

overview.title: The request-to-reply loop
overview.description: Read left to right. Every colored connector is a seam: green is proven, yellow is clean but unproven, red is intertwined, and blue is planned.

stages.label: External surfaces

stages.description: Authenticate, bind the agent, and turn the event into work.

stages.description: Claim delivery, lock the conversation, and resolve the run.

stages.description: Start or resume an isolated, steerable ACI session.

maturityRubric.label: Proven
maturityRubric.definition: Multiple real implementations have exercised the same boundary.

maturityRubric.label: Clean, unproven
maturityRubric.definition: One real implementation sits behind a credible boundary, but a second implementation has not tested the shape.

maturityRubric.label: Intertwined
maturityRubric.definition: A swap still requires coordinated knowledge or changes across implementation owners.

maturityRubric.label: Planned / reserved
maturityRubric.definition: The intended line is documented, but there is not a real implementation to score.

documentationDrift.title: ADR-0144 predates explicit namespace adoption
documentationDrift.claim: The draft ADR says there is no adopt flag and an operator must add created-owner labels manually.
documentationDrift.current: Explicit --adopt records the prior namespace contents and retains that namespace during teardown. Automatic adoption of an empty namespace can still assign deletion ownership.

documentationDrift.title: ADR-0144 predates the live schema assertion
documentationDrift.claim: The draft ADR says rollback has no override when the API pod cannot report its schema.
documentationDrift.current: The CLI accepts an operator-observed live schema revision while still enforcing the compatibility window before Helm mutates the release.

documentationDrift.title: ADR-0144 predates the quiesce-write fence
documentationDrift.claim: The draft ADR says the worker ignores a refused quiesce write and can strand its owned marker during cleanup.
documentationDrift.current: The worker checks the fenced write result, refuses the stale hook, and clears only the authoritative owned marker.

documentationDrift.title: ADRs 0125 and 0126 predate the installation level workspace gate
documentationDrift.claim: ADR 0125 specifies a nullable per-deployment repository; ADR 0126 replaces it with deployment workspace_enabled as the coding capability gate.
documentationDrift.current: The worker deliberately ignores that legacy deployment bit as a coding gate. The worker wide coordinator switch controls availability, while server scoped selection, the repository allowlist, and operator source bindings control workspace authority.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0144 predates the resumable upgrade driver
documentationDrift.claim: The draft leaves resumable checkpoints, convergence, canary proof and interrupted-phase recovery open.
documentationDrift.current: The CLI now resolves and pins a target chart, validates its version and schema metadata before mutation, owns a namespaced checkpoint through resource version compare and set, resumes nine phases, proves exact convergence, runs a target version canary, and records the observed known good version. This does not establish the distributed execution lease proposed by the ADR.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0173 predates implemented runner layering
documentationDrift.claim: ADR 0173 states that runner layering has no implementation.
documentationDrift.current: Bundles can build and select a layered runner with platform base validation. The release workflow now publishes the first party factory layer, and the renderer records layer and platform base digests.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0184 predates supervised stream retention
documentationDrift.claim: The Draft context says no production code runs XTRIM or XDEL on the consumed streams.
documentationDrift.current: The worker constructs and supervises StreamRetention, whose trim_settled pass runs XTRIM MINID below every consumer group settlement floor after the lag window. This does not establish the proposed Postgres receipts or counted-backlog changes.

documentationDrift.title: ADR 0203 predates argument-bound permission grants
documentationDrift.claim: Its context describes post-approval grants as tool-name scoped rather than argument scoped.
documentationDrift.current: Permission grants already require canonical equality with the stored approved argument object. This does not establish the planned remediation executor.

nodes.label: Slack
nodes.subtitle: Surface today
nodes.description: The original production channel. Bolt Socket Mode handles ingress; Slack Web API renders replies and approval cards. Progress rendering helpers exist, but deliberate progress delivery is disabled. It is no longer the only registered production kind. A streamed reply edit is cut to the 4,000 byte chat.update limit at a line break with a visible note. One installation can route several separate bot applications. Final replies and the stored progress outbox use stable delivery identity, and the receipt shown at turn end follows the installation mode.

nodes.label: Discord
nodes.subtitle: Shipped surface
nodes.description: Out-of-process Gateway adapter. Mentions in a bound parent channel create a public thread and placeholder; later thread messages continue the same conversation. v1 supports text, mentions, threads, and streamed edits. It does not implement buttons, DMs, attachments, or interactive approvals, and a Discord failure never falls back to Slack. The adapter now uses the shared telemetry bootstrap and redacting JSON logger for its own package plus discord.py, uvicorn, and httpx. OTLP export is supported, although the adapter still authors no spans or instruments.

nodes.label: Email
nodes.subtitle: Shipped surface
nodes.description: First-party AgentMail adapter with a scoped HTTP channel edge and threaded reply delivery. Current AgentMail inbound messages cannot establish sender authentication Curie can verify, so every message is refused with authentication_unverifiable before body fetching, starting a turn, or resolving an approval. Historical accepted deliveries can still receive one threaded reply per turn.completed. Delivery state is local SQLite with one serialized writer. Terminal completion rows compact oldest first under a derived cap without evicting unresolved or leased work, and an oversized database has an offline copy and VACUUM recovery command. Transport failures and all 4xx discovery refusals enter bounded backoff. Provider, channel, and egress credentials may come from per-field existing Secrets without chart ownership of their values. An external collector requires a narrow chart-declared egress peer.  The adapter uses shared telemetry and credential redaction, including OTLP export and startup-failure logs, without a generic environment-injection surface. Provider dialing stays within configured egress CIDRs while TLS verifies the provider hostname. Sustained discovery failure makes readiness fail after a bounded interval and appears in status; liveness stays independent and the Service retains reply delivery to the unready adapter. A refused provider TCP connection is classified separately during thread witness and send, returning a retryable 424 without treating it as a deleted thread or a completed delivery. An approval can be requested through email under the accepted route decision. Scoped approval-resolution authorization and email card delivery are implemented, but current inbound provider replies are refused before that resolution path. A live single use reference identifies the pending approval, while the platform checks the sender against binding callers and listed approvers. Requests go to existing thread participants; the adapter does not invite an absent approver itself. Replies in a thread with a pending approval do not start ordinary turns.

nodes.label: Teams
nodes.subtitle: Future surface
nodes.description: Named in the vision, but deliberately deferred until a real second channel teaches the adapter interface.

nodes.label: Curie CLI
nodes.subtitle: Agent-facing control
nodes.description: Drives skill, local, and cluster loops. The local/cluster message verbs can replace Slack ingress and reply transport without changing the worker path. Operators can mint and rotate row-scoped channel tokens, while status and doctor expose bounded completion-outbox and mail-delivery health without identifiers. The checkout-only release-accept evaluator reads a private evidence ledger and fails closed unless one unchanged candidate has seven days of accounted canaries and every recovery criterion. Push delivery diagnosis distinguishes configured, reachable, observed, and verified states instead of treating repository binding as delivery proof. A bare curie doctor discovers the platform API from cluster state, cluster up --dev preserves recorded comms and sealing values, and release builds embed the exact source commit used to resolve installer artifacts. Plain cluster up, apply, and diff retain installed typed mail settings, external Secret pairs, paired worker adapter credentials, and installed local inference. Explicit namespace adoption records prior labels and objects, and cluster down retains the adopted namespace. Hosted connector deploys wait for current revision readiness; skill and local connector startup share one configurable bounded deadline. Explicit source decisions take precedence without replaying stale inline credentials. Offline dry-run plans do not read an installed release. Cluster up and apply wait for the installed Helm target workloads to converge; cluster status returns failure with redacted generation, replica, image and hook diagnoses when the target is unhealthy. Cluster upgrade resolves the selected release chart or explicit local/ref target, pins it to the requested version, validates declared chart version and rendered target schema metadata before mutation, and requires explicit forward-only admission for pending contract or irreversible migrations. One namespaced ConfigMap owns the operation and its durable nine-phase checkpoint through resourceVersion and holder compare-and-set. A resumed upgrade proves exact target images, generations, replicas, hooks, queues, and manifest state, then runs a target-version canary and records known-good from the observed release version. The CLI rollback catalog for v0.9.0 spans migrations 0001 through 0044; it is distinct from the API image serving compatibility window of 0044 through 0044. The 0.9.2 and 0.9.3 release identities each carry the exact 0045 through 0045 schema window because no migration landed between them. CI refuses a new migration unless the release windows advance consistently. The restore and upgrade drills exercise stable installation survival and recovery. Sibling tag image reports require a unique serving Node inventory binding and conditional Node read; this does not prove mutable tag freshness. An explicit cluster context pins every Helm and kubectl child. Channel token operations refuse failed release discovery instead of guessing a Secret name. Retained up escapes literal dotted object keys, while upgrade preserves scalar types through JSON values. Ambiguous 0.8.8 and 0.8.9 rollback identities require retained schema metadata. Local commands and ladder runs honor explicit Compose project and endpoint settings. The 0.10.0 and 0.10.1 release identities share schema window 0045 through 0058. A bundle deploy leaves the platform release alone unless a connector secret name is new or its value changed. Worker status and doctor report a paused fleet's remaining quiesce TTL, and the example sre-bot provision-observability verb records a receipt naming the Grafana connector Secret without the token. The v0.11.0 candidate uses API schema 0070; the historical release windows remain separately recorded for upgrade admission. The 0.11.2 release identity carries schema window 0070 through 0070. Upgrade refuses absent or partial caller credential pairs before mutation, including dry run, same version verification, and resume; upgrade does not generate a missing pair. Budget updates preserve unspecified values. Factory rendering selects the published runner layer and emits a strict version 2 receipt with required bundle_dir, rendered, runner_image, and runner_note fields. The runner fields accept string or null, unknown fields are rejected, the schema ID ends in /v2.json, and its index version is 2.0. The App completion path explicitly selects factory polling without requiring a webhook secret. Operators can control memory writes and guidance. Factory render receipt schema v2 requires nullable runner_image and runner_note fields. Local and cluster Console login commands discover the installation credential and mint a subject-bound single-use login code. Cluster up retains recorded runner environment and credential references; cluster upgrade deletes removed runner layers instead of setting them to null. Controller reuse checks rollout health and the chart image for an unowned controller. A missing rendered RuntimeClass is read before install: NotFound can infer gVisor off, while Forbidden preserves the exact admission retry. Release tooling can reuse complete green first-parent checks only across a version-only delta; the proposed combined preparation-head authorization remains Draft. Checkout-only developer preflight checks committed content and fetched base freshness, reports failing required base checks, and runs selected cheap CI gates. The full tier selects affected Python workspace members and transitive dependents, using four xdist workers with loadgroup scheduling. Service-dependent checks own private backing services, loopback endpoints, a private runner network and the matching released-upgrade isolation contract, with verified teardown on success, failure and interruption. The fast tier runs service-free gates and substitutes cargo check --locked --tests for CI cargo test --locked. Install, update and hook installation configure relative core.hooksPath=.githooks; the tracked pre-push hook checks each pushed ref tip from that commit. Remaining parity and kind checks are reported as CI-only. Hook fire succeeds only for the durable ran outcome; failed, blocked, skipped and reclaimed outcomes fail while preserving the record and reason. Open runs remain polled until settlement or a transient timeout naming the same-tier record command. Hook record reads an existing run without waiting or judging its outcome. Schedule reads separate newest scheduled and manual histories. Deploy schema v1.2 always includes cron declarations and advisory warnings from the immutable uploaded bundle; unresolved explicit targets warn after successful deployment. Cluster teardown bounds owned namespace deletion to 300 seconds, preserves finalizers, and reports remaining phase, conditions, objects and an exact resume command. A remaining owned namespace yields a transient failure unless an independent permanent teardown failure takes precedence. The v0.12.2 release identity and candidate serving window are 0076 through 0081; historical v0.12.1 remains 0076 through 0076. The v0.12.3 release catalog and API serving window are 0076 through 0093. Released windows are checked against their release tag while the candidate may advance; rollback declared-window checks use the next catalogued release head as an upper bound and leave the newest release unbounded.

nodes.label: GitHub
nodes.subtitle: Push / PR trigger
nodes.description: Webhook and outbound commit polling converge on the API git-flow engine. Dev pushes build and evaluate; production pushes promote. Repository binding is not delivery proof: pushes arrive through either an operator-created webhook or configured commit polling, and Curie reports only observed configuration rather than claiming that exposure proves delivery. The platform also clones managed workspaces and publishes through an approval-gated path that never leaves write credentials inside the sandbox. One scoped thread and repository own one fenced pull request lineage. Human issue comments, pull request review comments, and submitted reviews are admitted only for the currently open bound pull request after fresh provider reads confirm the immutable repository, installation, pull request, binding generation, and exact head. Accepted feedback enters a durable outbox for the original scoped thread; stale heads, terminal pull requests, unavailable provider truth, and authority mismatches start no model turn. Signed labelled issue events now admit one canonical factory WorkItem, while relabel, unlabel, issue comments, and review events retain distinct authority checks. Factory status and final outcome comments use the GitHub issue as their operator surface. Because GitHub does not redeliver a failed webhook, the API reconciler also polls bound repositories for factory labelled issues with no WorkItem and admits them with a request identity derived from the labeled event. Factory state labels moved to the curie-factory prefix. Covered factory publication turns can compare a proposed title and body against a fresh API side pull request read without any GitHub credential entering the sandbox. Factory intake now defaults to outbound polling with optional webhook delivery. The platform reads the issue through a scoped capability with its own fresh App token; the factory sandbox needs no GitHub read credential.

nodes.label: External hook
nodes.subtitle: HMAC-triggered turn
nodes.description: A named, HMAC-authenticated API hook creates a quota- and body-bounded webhook-sourced turn whose authenticated payload is escaped and delimited as untrusted prompt content. For alert-driven coding, an operator-owned source binding extracts a configured workload fact and maps it to an allowlisted repository plus recorded revision. Missing, ambiguous, malformed, or unauthorized mappings refuse before workspace selection, and payload URLs never choose the target. Declared cron schedules ship; deploy wiring for declared generic webhooks remains planned. A hook may explicitly request tool_access=read-only. Its receipt proves the queued policy only; an operator must establish compatible worker and runner artifacts because the API does not discover homogeneous fleet enforcement. An authenticated hook may select a preposted reply context under the signed request contract. Signed ingress now repeats authentication under a dedicated live SQL source gate. Configured policy or durable operation history refuses the ordinary path before delivery effects. Hook-specific signing, source control, broker metadata and atomic protected admission primitives exist, but protected provisioning, worker consumption and qualified runtime execution are not wired into this route. Protected admission recovery rereads concurrent commit observations within a 32-attempt bound while retaining stable orphan refusal.

nodes.label: Console UI
nodes.subtitle: Operations surface
nodes.description: A real API-backed console for fleet, runs, metrics, cost, logs, versions, evals, approvals, and memory. Approval resolution uses the authenticated Console session subject rather than a caller-supplied actor. Usage and Settings remain honest stubs. An external API requires an explicit proxy target; chart rendering refuses a disabled in-chart API without that target. Agent cards and the Overview card show each agent's runs, tokens, and cost from the metrics summary, and show unknown cost when the model has no price. Console session creation and reads have separate shared Valkey budgets. The browser now authenticates only with the HttpOnly Console session cookie. A single-use CLI-minted login code is exchanged for that session; protected views mount only after the session probe succeeds, and a protected request returning 401 returns the UI to sign-in. Browser configuration and API requests no longer carry the platform administrator key. Cookie-authenticated mutations require a matching origin. Its other session-authenticated API calls are ordinary control-plane traffic; the map draws only the trace and metrics read path, which belongs to the telemetry seam, and attributes no seam to the generic traffic.

nodes.label: Dispatcher
nodes.subtitle: Ingress · dedupe · placeholder
nodes.description: Before Socket Mode, a bounded startup preflight waits for API health and verifies configured Slack destination capabilities. The live dispatcher then normalizes Slack events and Block Kit text into QueuedTurn, carries adapter scoped file references without downloading their bytes, records adapter owned refusals, deduplicates ingress, posts the placeholder, and appends to the run stream. Bot authored thread messages are admitted only for explicitly trusted bot and channel pairs. Approval clicks become independently signed, approval bound chat principal attestations; an exact record miss is treated as another release owning that approval, never as authority to mutate it. Its single Deployment replica uses a Recreate rollout so Socket Mode never runs two clients on one app token; Slack retries delivery across the reconnect gap. One installation can now run several declared Slack identities and route each event through its owning application. A binding caller list is checked before a placeholder or turn is created. For a threaded mention, a bounded lookup verifies this bot authored the root and quotes it as untrusted context with slashes neutralized; that context grants no new routing authority. Configured and connected Socket Mode identity counts are measured independently of the process heartbeat.

nodes.label: Port adapter service
nodes.subtitle: Third-party channel edge
nodes.description: The accepted placement for a generic third-party adapter kit: a deployed service, not a bundle-loaded plugin. Slack, Discord, and email already ship as first-party surfaces. The generic adapter manifest, install flow, service discovery, and conformance kit remain unbuilt.

nodes.label: Channel HTTP edge
nodes.subtitle: Generic ingress + egress
nodes.description: The API mints row-scoped channel tokens and platform-owned QueuedTurn records; every mint increments the row generation before signing, so reminting immediately revokes the prior token. A separately scoped adapter principal can rotate its own credential, mint channel tokens only for bindings it serves, list approvals on those routes, and resolve eligible explicit-user approvals. Discord and email already consume this HTTP edge. Worker-side HttpReplyAdapter posts the four versioned reply events to each binding's server-controlled endpoint, while the reserved built-in cluster-message relay returns CLI-driven replies through the API. TurnIn carries Attachment references onto the queue. Non Slack references are resolved at the binding's attachment endpoint through ChannelPortFileClient with the adapter egress credential; Discord and mail still emit no references. In a disconnected cluster relay, adapter selects reply delivery while optional ReplyHandle.identity selects the named Slack binding; unknown identities refuse.

nodes.label: API
nodes.subtitle: Control plane · git flow
nodes.description: Owns agents, versions, deployments, multi-surface channel bindings, approvals, state, connector rendering, managed repository workspaces, bundle validation, git flow deploys, and read proxies. Scoped thread workspace identity, one active thread and repository pull request lineage, publication revision reservations, GitHub review authority, delivery audit, and the durable feedback outbox are control-plane state. Source bindings let operators map alert workload facts to an allowlisted repository and recorded revision without trusting payload URLs. Bundle archive validation runs outside the API event loop. Readiness exercises the same list agents query as the public endpoint, while liveness stays process local, so a database state that breaks normal reads removes the pod from service without restarting it. The v0.12.0 release catalog and target API declare schema 0070 through 0073, retaining the memory, factory base and polling cursor migrations. A version cannot become live when its bundle declares an approval route that the agent has not bound, and a live binding cannot be removed underneath that declaration. Approval resolution authenticates chat, Console, operator, or scoped adapter principals; the platform key alone cannot resolve. An opt-in break-glass route can report approval identity gaps and reject a stranded approval with an atomic audit entry and ordinary resume event. A transcript over its per-thread cap increments a bounded value-limit counter, state namespace capacity refusals have their own counters, and readiness remains independent of data capacity. Signed factory issue intake, durable WorkItems and ExecutionRequests, a leased status comment outbox, observed CI state, explicit publication policy, and outcome routes are API owned. Per thread transcripts moved from the shared state namespace to a dedicated capped table with terminal and idle expiry. For a covered factory turn with an open lineage, a worker authenticated route mints a signed publication precheck capability, and a separate scoped route performs one fresh pull request read, compares metadata, and charges a shared Valkey budget of twenty attempts per lineage in five minutes; it cannot create approval or publication state. The WorkItem reconciler also lists open factory labelled issues on bound repositories and admits a lost label delivery through the webhook verification path after a grace period. Factory state labels use the curie-factory prefix, the CI wait is an operator setting, CI repair prompts carry bounded redacted GitHub Actions job log tails, and queued status comments report an installation upgrade pause. The API records bot identities and binding caller policy, reports factory usage, and serves approval route decisions from the recorded request location. Its approval record remains the authority when a card is settled. Action completion and undo acquisition use conditional SQL writes so stale loaded rows cannot complete or authorize restore twice. Redacted action snapshots retain neither prior nor post state and cannot support undo. Successful state deletes and operator memory edits and deletes emit content free operation logs and bounded mutation counts; no value or memory content enters those observations. Requester display follows only a validated approval resume chain and does not change grant or resolution authority. Factory issue and comment reads use an execution scoped route and fresh App installation tokens owned by the API. Live execution and lease authority are validated around provider reads, and bounded Valkey attempts limit access. Canonical factory verification observations gate publication, and one Actions rerun on the exact current head precedes CI repair. Console session creation and reads use separate shared Valkey budgets. Factory polling uses durable Postgres cursors and one advisory lock across replicas. It sends observations through the existing verification and admission path. Memory authority is checked at the state API: a sandbox can read only its own channel memory and needs a turn credential for fact writes; the server records the author. Transcript scope is also checked against the binding. Progress commands enter a generation scoped durable inbox, with rendering disabled. A live Console session now authenticates ordinary administrative API requests; cookie-authenticated mutations enforce same-origin authority. Hook source policy and immutable operation history are durable SQL state. Signed hook authentication is repeated under a dedicated agent-scoped source gate, whose continued liveness is checked before effects. Any configured source policy or operation history closes the current ordinary ingress path. Source administration and mutation coordinators exist as internal primitives, without a complete protected HTTP delivery path. Startup probes require readable source-policy and operation structures before runtime construction. Failed resume enqueues observed by the current API process are retried on the next reconciler pass. The process record is capped at 10,000 approvals; restart loss and failures beyond that cap retain the grace backstop. A short locked transaction enqueues before marking resumed and retains still-owed locked rows for another pass. Scheduled and manual hook runs have independent histories and nullable terminal reason codes. Per-agent reviewer_model is nullable; explicit null clears it while omission preserves it. The candidate API and shared serving window are 0076 through 0081. When head checks fail, factory CI reads the current base branch head within the remaining observation budget. Matching failing check names or status contexts are reported as pre-existing and excluded from repair, but required Python or delegated checks failing on that base remain unverified. An unreadable base makes every head failure count as caused. A refused factory publication snapshot ends with approval_create_failed and carries the existing redacted, clipped refusal detail into the issue Details line. A sanitized-base mismatch names the first 12 hexadecimal characters of both snapshot and prepared commits; repository mismatch wording and refusal behavior remain unchanged. Publication prose reports CI at pull request creation time and points to the issue status comment for subsequent results. An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries. Factory status synchronization owns a versioned SQL lease, releases database sessions before GitHub I/O, and runs separately from dispatch reconciliation. Late matching runtime heartbeats may renew before the execution deadline, with one heartbeat-TTL grace before owner-loss cancellation. Verification replay preserves the first observation for an unchanged command. CI reports unavailable required check names and merge_conflict explicitly instead of waiting for checks GitHub will not start. Factory metadata CI admission is an operator-controlled chart value. The v0.12.3 candidate serving window is 0076 through 0093; v0.12.2 remains 0076 through 0081.

nodes.label: Valkey streams
nodes.subtitle: Runs · evals · delivery
nodes.description: At-least-once streams carry run and eval jobs. Shared consumer machinery provides bounded delivery, a renewable fenced owner per delivery, lease-expiry recovery, and dead-letter handling. Conversation locks are stamped with consumer ownership and can transfer only after capability plus sustained missing-alive proof. The same bounded graveyard also retains terminal completion-outbox failures, which are not replayable inbound entries. An external Valkey can require TLS; one shared chart helper keeps all seven consumers on the same transport and refuses TLS for the in-chart broker without a TLS listener. Interactive turns now park in a durable capacity wait when a sandbox cannot start. A fixed deadline, generation fence, wake reconciliation, and terminal notice prevent an unbounded or silently lost wait; the runner grants admission to the exact waiting turn epoch before input is sent. The supervised retention loop trims entries older than its lag window only below every consumer group settlement floor. Protected broker metadata transport, permission roles and atomic admission with bounded recovery are implemented as internal primitives; a complete separately deployed protected delivery endpoint and consumer remain planned. Delivery and consumer liveness renewals tolerate transport errors only until the last confirmed send plus TTL minus one heartbeat interval. A refused renewal loses authority immediately. Side-effect markers retry before applying the frame, and terminal settlement remains fenced. Runs and evals share this ownership rule.

nodes.label: Worker kernel
nodes.subtitle: Route · claim · steer · recover
nodes.description: The concurrency hub: resolves the active deployment, emits a typed terminal failure instead of dropping turns when none exists, enforces one live session per scoped conversation, selects steer versus fresh turn, and protects side effects. It resolves channel attachment references through the selected Slack file client or ChannelPortFileClient. The latter fetches opaque ids from the binding endpoint with its adapter egress credential; accepted bytes are stored under a private prefix and exposed through a short lived signed redemption reference before sandbox claim. Managed coding uses the canonical scoped thread identity rather than a bare reply id. The worker selects and sanitizes an allowlisted repository checkout, archives it privately, and swaps a late workspace into the route only at a fenced turn boundary; multiple ambiguous bare owner/repo-like tokens leave repository selection absent, while multiple explicit repository URLs are refused. Review turns never steer a live sandbox: fresh authority is verified again, the exact accepted pull request head is reserved and materialized, and a replacement sandbox cold-claims that checkout. Publication validates a revision against its base, captures the immutable GitHub repository, installation, and pull request node identities in the same write that opens the pull request, creates a fresh approval, and reconciles approved work through the same pull request lineage; stale, terminal, unavailable, or mismatched authority is refused before model or write work. Runs, evals, kill switch, heartbeat, connector, publication, and completion loops are individually supervised with exponential backoff; a repeatedly crashing loop is parked after a bounded streak while siblings continue. Terminal reply events enter a durable, generation fenced completion outbox before the done marker; independent bounded sweeps retry delivery and quarantine expired or malformed records. Each runner request is capped by both the configured runner ceiling and the delivery's remaining deadline. Upgrade drain refuses a fenced quiesce write and holds its quiesce marker as a short lease renewed while the gate waits, so a killed or deleted gate releases the fleet within one lease; SIGTERM and SIGINT clear it. Runner error classifications are allowlisted across runner and worker; escalation detail is redacted before it reaches either the user reply or logs. Generic turns still execute with repository workspaces disabled; named repository requests, verified review feedback, and retained repository sessions refuse before execution. Retained generic attachment turns replace only an authenticated idle runner with durable history through an exact claim and generation fence. Repository attachment replacement remains deferred. One bounded idle route reclamation follows a proven ResourceQuota refusal and retries only after exact quota headroom is observed. Idle eval routes are reclaimed ahead of person routes while preserving expiry order inside each group. Approval resume also attempts idle reclamation before returning sandbox-capacity, provided the same quota evidence and deadline permit it. The effective runner timeout bounds the whole stream; unconfirmed timeout ownership ends terminally instead of retrying. The factory dispatcher acquires durable requests before starting a turn, waits on capacity, reconciles orphaned runs, observes cancellation, and rotates CI repair rounds without losing the WorkItem. A declared cron trigger is claimed once per slot in SQL and enqueued onto the same bounded run stream. Factory execution is capped by its three hour deadline and an explicit turn budget. Before each covered factory execute or CI turn, including warm runner reuse and continuations, the worker requests fresh publication precheck context from the API and binds it to the ACI Event; if minting fails it stops before starting the turn. A streaming turn refreshes its live route and workspace lease every third of the route TTL. An unpublished factory execute turn gets one continuation, and a factory execution whose claimed pod is Unschedulable at the claim timeout defers as capacity instead of failing. Slack edits are cut to the 4,000 byte chat.update limit and receipts list at most ten actions. Interactive turns now park in a durable capacity wait when a sandbox cannot start. A fixed deadline, generation fence, wake reconciliation, and terminal notice prevent an unbounded or silently lost wait; the runner grants admission to the exact waiting turn epoch before input is sent. A failed runner turn produces a marked channel reply and a failed message result, with distinct causes for exhausted turns and unclassified failures. The worker carries the selected bot identity through reply delivery, mints a signed connector caller token for the agent at sandbox boot, and reports factory usage. The progress store now persists one fenced, bounded record per logical turn chain and an idempotent card and milestone outbox in Valkey. A scoped model command ingress and worker pumps apply chain state; rendering remains disabled and no adapter delivers that outbox. The maintenance sweep can quarantine pending records. A disconnected cluster message keeps its reserved internal relay adapter after the Slack binding resolves, so its reply returns to the CLI instead of real Slack. The installation chooses whether terminal replies include all, failed, or no action receipts. Turns that the worker cannot start because capacity is unavailable, an attachment cannot be fetched, or the agent has no pool receive a terminal reply and count as classified failures in turn telemetry, not completed work. Restricted turns run only after the exact runner advertises enforcement; they never steer a live session or obtain a connector approval grant. A dropped stream is classified sandbox-terminated only when pod_termination confirms the exact Kubernetes pod or a matching recent event, otherwise it remains a transport failure; Docker supplies no termination evidence. Redacted action results retain neither prior nor post state and cannot promise undo. A card whose approval resolved before registration is settled immediately after registration. Thread reset records released or no route in a one hour Valkey result before clearing the in progress marker. The API exposes whether a route existed; the CLI refuses a no route result and the UI reports that nothing was released. Failed teardown stays pending and emits a failed lifecycle outcome. A fresh request clears the prior result. For a factory execution the worker mints and injects the issue read route and execution scoped wir capability. Terminal budget notices distinguish exhausted output tokens from the USD limit. The worker sends channel memory references even when writes are off, and supplies write authority per turn only when enabled. Turn closure revokes that authority, with credential expiry as the backstop. Eligible human Slack turns receive leased progress capabilities; a live pump and maintenance drainer apply the same durable inbox. No progress deliverer is enabled. Scheduled ordinary admission now holds task-owned source authority and rechecks its liveness before claims, queue writes and failure effects; configured policy or history refuses that path. Startup validates readable source authority structures and owns the separate source-gate resources through shutdown. Claim-scoped boot state credentials carry one credential id and a bounded expiry; claim deletion reports release, retaining failed reports for retry. Per-turn memory writes expire at the delivery deadline without grace, and the owning live turn closes its attempt credentials. A text-only follow-up can hand a fresh sandbox the newest retained attachment set for the same thread and agent. The worker remints short-lived object references without extending retention; missing, near-expiry or malformed sets are omitted, and the best-effort lookup is bounded to five seconds. Every newly created claim receives a fresh boot credential id, preventing replacement or retry claims from reusing a released credential while preserving agent, scope and expiry. Ordinary and eval boots forward reviewer_model. Hook settlement records a terminal reason, and model-usage-limited is distinct from credit exhaustion. A refused factory publication snapshot ends with approval_create_failed and carries the existing redacted, clipped refusal detail into the issue Details line. A sanitized-base mismatch names the first 12 hexadecimal characters of both snapshot and prepared commits; repository mismatch wording and refusal behavior remain unchanged. Publication prose reports CI at pull request creation time and points to the issue status comment for subsequent results. Delivery and consumer liveness renewals tolerate transport errors only until the last confirmed send plus TTL minus one heartbeat interval. A refused renewal loses authority immediately. Side-effect markers retry before applying the frame, and terminal settlement remains fenced. Runs and evals share this ownership rule. An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries. Publication snapshots accumulate the response through EOF under the encoded and decoded size limits. Retryable read faults receive at most three reads within the remaining budget, without rerunning the model. Exhaustion names infrastructure read failure in the issue. Idempotent publication creation and execution settlement writes retry transient API faults within bounded authority; unresolved terminal reports retain heartbeat and sandbox ownership until settlement or the execution deadline. Charged publication reconciliation retries back off from fifteen seconds to five minutes.

nodes.label: Approval plane
nodes.subtitle: Durable human gate
nodes.description: A gate terminates the turn as AWAITING_APPROVAL, persists a durable record and its validated originating trace context, suspends the sandbox, and later resumes through a new queued resolution turn that continues that trace when available. The runner's PreToolUse hook is the primary permission gate and can_use_tool is its backstop. Configuration-time checks refuse a declared-but-unbound approval route before deployment or route mutation, while request-time checks remain the fail-safe. Legacy or malformed carriers intentionally start a clean root. The resume reconciler's grace is derived from the delivery budget plus shutdown reserve. Resolution accepts only authenticated chat, Console, operator, or scoped adapter principals and checks every principal, including the requester, against the captured approver set. An adapter can see and resolve only approvals served by its binding set, and only through explicit user routes. When multiple releases share one Slack app, only the API owning the approval record may resolve it. One resolution target owns the sole interactive card. An optional pager target receives text only, with no ConfirmIntent, action value, or remembered card reference, so it cannot create a second approval card or authority path. Publication approval is fresh for each proposed revision, never resumes the model directly, and review feedback is not itself an approval. Known read-only tools avoid approval and receipt side effects. Durable authority is recorded before any card or notice delivery, including turns without an existing reply reference. Publication cards preserve the CLI reply adapter and a stable pending lifetime. The shipped SRE gates, including mcp__curie__publish_changes, carry sre-approvals; explicit user bindings allow operator resolution without Slack transport. A separately granted administrative recovery path can reject and audit a stranded approval without widening the ordinary membership decision. For covered factory turns, the runner resolves an empty publication proposal before any path records pending publication state: blank body, local head drift, no change, stale context, unavailable comparison, and metadata only proposals return nonhalting refusals, while a real file change still takes the mandatory approval gate. Admission remains the independent authority check. A permission approval persists the denied call's canonical argument object and binds the one use resume grant to that same tool and argument object. Concurrent delivery copies of one resume event are fenced by an event claim tied to the active delivery lease. Session approvals have a 24 hour deadline. A card resolves at the location where its request was asked, and the requester thread receives notices in order. A settled card records the decision while the durable approval row remains authoritative. Email resolution is specified but its adapter implementation remains pending. The displayed requester is recovered only from a validated resume chain and never participates in authorization. When a decision precedes card registration, successful registration immediately checks durable authority and settles the card. Failed resume enqueues observed by the current API process are retried on the next reconciler pass. The process record is capped at 10,000 approvals; restart loss and failures beyond that cap retain the grace backstop. A short locked transaction enqueues before marking resumed and retains still-owed locked rows for another pass.

nodes.label: Eval plane
nodes.subtitle: Cases · graders · report
nodes.description: The same bundle-carried eval suite runs across skill, local, local-release, and cluster. Worker scores and records cases, then reports a rollup to the API.

nodes.label: Sandbox
nodes.subtitle: One isolated session
nodes.description: An isolated runtime claimed per conversation. Kubernetes Agent Sandbox is production; Docker runs the same image locally. Accepted inbound files appear read only under /attachments on both substrates. Managed repository content appears at /workspace from a private signed one-object reference and digest; GitHub and object-store credentials never enter the runner. Kubernetes redeems references in dedicated credentialless init containers, while Docker redeems them in the substrate driver. A late workspace or accepted review replaces the route only at a fenced turn boundary, and review work starts from the exact verified pull request head in a newly claimed sandbox. Session identity can arrive over the ACI so a warm pool sandbox may be prebound before the turn. Chart render fails closed if the retired in path LiteLLM sidecar is reenabled (ADR-0037). Retained attachment replacement preserves the logical session and transcript while cold creating a candidate before detaching the old route. Capacity, binding, or fence failure preserves the old claim. Quota pressure can reclaim at most one safe idle route and does not add a background scheduler. Package registry egress is closed by default; an agent listed under agentSandbox.registryEgress gets its own NetworkPolicy and a labeled per agent sandbox pool that the worker routes its claims to. A claim whose pod the scheduler cannot place is reported as unschedulable so factory work can defer for capacity. Kubernetes refuses a connector secret claim before scheduling if the chart rendered no secret capable agent pool. Local Docker has no warm pool and carries those secrets directly into its runner claim. Transient Kubernetes reads are treated as no observation while a claim binds. Claim timeout captures a bounded redacted runner log tail before cleanup; Docker offers no Kubernetes log-tail evidence.

nodes.label: Runner / ACI server
nodes.subtitle: Multi-turn session loop
nodes.description: Serves event, steer, interrupt, timeout, reset, and snapshot; translates harness events into the frozen NDJSON union; injects memory and history; and probes MCP capabilities conservatively. For hosted Bearer connectors, the runner expands the named secret into the in memory MCP header, removes that name from the process environment, and writes the full MCP configuration to a mode 0600 file instead of the Claude process argv. Missing or empty credentials still halt before a model call with a names only diagnosis. A failed capability probe is retried inside each later accepted turn; a persistent probe failure denies that connector's tools and reports the condition while still running the model. The disallowed tool list blocks named tools rather than the underlying credential backed capability. Permission enforcement layers a primary PreToolUse hook with a can_use_tool backstop, and runner local disallowed tool policy applies to both real and fake sessions. Bundle command hooks run from the mounted plugin root with CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT set; exit 2 denies, while exit 0 stdout can return a deny, ask, or stop decision. Telemetry records each observed provider wait and tool wait interval as root siblings with bounded phase, terminal, round, TTFT, and outcome attributes. Portable structured history preserves ordered messages and tool results, with optional native checkpoints for cache reuse. Appends reserve room for durable publication outcomes. On a capacity refusal the runner compacts through versioned compare-and-set, preserves publication markers and the newest turn, reloads on conflicts, and retries. Only a capacity refusal that survives bounded compaction replaces success or approval with history-persistence-error and CLASSIFIED_FAILURE; ordinary append failures retain the outcome but mark durability lost. Boot uses the same bounded compaction and reload path before accepting a turn. For a covered factory turn, one per turn publication decision is shared by the stream observer, PreToolUse hook, and can_use_tool, keyed by the exact tool call identity. An empty working tree snapshot is compared through the API precheck endpoint, accepted only at the boot delivered trusted origin, without redirects, within ten seconds and at most five times per turn; refusals are nonhalting and record no pending approval. The runner reads the transcript value cap the state API advertises and can replace older completed tool exchanges within one long turn with a deterministic marker. Every SDK session disables commit and pull request attribution text. The turn start log is emitted inside agent.run so even a successful turn without tools has a runner log with the turn trace context. Hosted Kubernetes connector requests carry a worker signed cct to the mandatory caller proxy, with a separate one use ccg for an approval gated connector tool. The runner reports measured usage for factory accounting and keeps a checkpoint only under the matching system prompt. ACI 0.5.9 adds optional per turn read only enforcement. Tools outside the declared read only set, including approval requiring tools, are denied before approval or registered callback work; restricted steers and slash commands refuse. A prior unrestricted SDK session cannot accept a restricted prompt, and the first unrestricted prompt after a restricted turn replaces that SDK session. Portable history preserves proven assistant message grouping and refuses ambiguous overlapping tool calls; replay may reduce an independently isolatable ambiguous old turn to its visible text. Each boot's attachment notice is added to its first actual prompt and persisted with that message, preserving reattachment under an unchanged filename. Text block paragraph separators are placed after whole text redaction so they cannot split a held secret, and final redaction preserves the same boundaries. The current ACI version is 0.5.15. Per turn memory write authority is carried on the Event, while boot memory credentials remain read only. The platform get_issue tool uses the boot supplied issue read route and execution scoped capability. Credential variables are removed from Bash and hook environments before shell startup. SDK error subtypes produce classified terminal failures even when is_error is false, and usage accounting subtracts prior cumulative SDK totals. Agent and channel facts load with recorded authors even when writes are off. Enabled memory tools can remember, update and forget facts using the turn credential, with a bounded fact count. The harness exposes only the bundle skill list. Its platform progress tool uses a scoped API capability rather than the ACI event stream. Serving requires a nonblank bearer token unless the explicit development tokenless flag is set. Channel-bound turns hide SendMessage and PushNotification. A blocked declared verification check selects an offline PreflightBlockedSession before model startup and reports zero implementer usage. Reviewer credit exhaustion is terminal for the whole turn, and measured factory usage separates implementer and reviewer totals. ACI 0.5.15 adds optional BootEnv.reviewer_model, forwarded as CURIE_REVIEWER_MODEL. Local and cluster overrides can pin or clear it. Ordinary and eval boots forward the per-agent value; omission preserves the override and explicit null clears it. Without an override the runner resolves the SDK Opus alias from the effective credential. Factory quickstart selects a provider-appropriate implementer default for Anthropic or OpenRouter credentials while preserving an explicit model. Provider subscription usage refusals have a distinct terminal model-usage-limited classification, take precedence over credit refusals and interrupt before SDK retries or parent continuation. An OpenRouter key spend-limit 403 remains credit exhaustion. Budget accounting counts a repeated assistant response id once per turn. Factory usage pairs base model observations with a unique context-window-suffixed aggregate key and avoids counting already reported reviewer usage twice; API pricing strips the trailing context suffix before matching rates. Turns ending without a ResultMessage report the observed token counts once; draining a later abandoned result advances the usage baseline without reporting those tokens again. A classified terminal failure that stores no transcript terminal can authorize durable replacement when no earlier history loss remains.

nodes.label: Claude harness
nodes.subtitle: Declared package today
nodes.description: The only production harness contribution. ModelSession exists, but raw SDK messages and the Claude Code plugin format still cross the conceptual boundary. Draft ADR-0140 would stop the speculative multi-harness program until a real second engine exists; while Draft, it authorizes no change to the accepted harness contracts.

nodes.label: Model endpoint
nodes.subtitle: Provider-selected inference
nodes.description: Anthropic is the default; OpenRouter, Zhipu, Moonshot, DeepSeek, and opt-in Ollama routes are also built. Cluster Ollama pulls now require an explicit durable-storage policy or a declaration that weights are pre-provisioned; ephemeral implicit downloads are refused before mutation. Native OpenAI wire format remains absent. ACI 0.5.15 adds optional BootEnv.reviewer_model, forwarded as CURIE_REVIEWER_MODEL. Local and cluster overrides can pin or clear it. Ordinary and eval boots forward the per-agent value; omission preserves the override and explicit null clears it. Without an override the runner resolves the SDK Opus alias from the effective credential. Factory quickstart selects a provider-appropriate implementer default for Anthropic or OpenRouter credentials while preserving an explicit model.

nodes.label: MCP connector hosts
nodes.subtitle: Collapsed MCP implementations
nodes.description: Bundle declared hosted, source built, remote, and unhosted fallback MCP implementations remain collapsed behind this role. Cluster deploy waits for each hosted Deployment's current revision to become ready or fails with a bounded redacted diagnosis. Skill and local startup use a separate Docker host outside the connector port and share one configurable bounded readiness deadline. The platform separately warns when a hosted workload has no mounted MCP entry. Runner boot performs the actual MCP capability and authentication probe, then later turns may retry a transient probe failure without redialing missing credentials. Renderer and CLI now share a frozen derived Bearer selection rule. Draft ADR-0158 documents a bundle-built HTTP MCP server that owns its provider credential, based on retained historical spike evidence, but it authorizes no new product surface. Hosted connector Deployments now expose TCP readiness on their MCP port. Several upstream SecretRef credentials are accepted without inventing a client Bearer header; skill and local tiers stage an explicitly derived Bearer credential when one is declared. Every hosted Kubernetes connector requires a caller proxy and public key; the API refuses a missing pair with 422. The proxy verifies a signed cct with agent and exp claims and optional paired run and work item claims, then enforces the declared admits policy. Approval gated tool calls additionally require a separate signed ccg matching agent, connector, tool, canonical arguments, expiry, and a jti spent once through Valkey. Skill and local startup require a caller public key and generate an ephemeral pair, but their Docker host runs the original connector image directly and enforces neither caller tokens nor connector grants. Upgrade refuses an absent or partial caller credential pair before mutation rather than generating one; cluster up can generate a missing pair. The caller proxy verifies optional paired run and work item claims and derives their forwarded headers from the signed caller token. The test environment connector requires this pair before creating a namespace.

nodes.label: MCP OAuth gateway
nodes.subtitle: Per-person delegated access
nodes.description: The accepted vision boundary for delegated MCP authorization. The control plane owns OAuth discovery, PKCE, encrypted tokens, refresh, revocation, and grants; the gateway applies the active run principal's grant without exposing raw OAuth tokens to the runner.

nodes.label: Agent Proxy
nodes.subtitle: Credentials + egress boundary
nodes.description: Accepted architecture moves provider credentials and enforceable egress policy out of the sandbox. The direction is decided, but substrate, TLS termination, credential injection, and implementation remain follow-up work.

nodes.label: OTel collector
nodes.subtitle: Telemetry write port
nodes.description: Receives OTLP from Curie services and the runner and exports to Langfuse over HTTP. Ingress, durable approval resolution, expiry, and reconciliation preserve the originating W3C trace context when valid; missing or malformed legacy carriers start clean roots. Request path operation spans may carry curie.channel.event_id from a task local scope, while metrics reject that unbounded identifier and maintenance work outside the request scope remains unstamped. The runner emits truthful sibling provider and tool phase intervals with a closed versioned attribute set; the collector boundary remains mostly vendor neutral. Chart CI discovers first party workloads from rendered images and rejects a new workload without the shared OTLP environment. Discord independently bootstraps the same telemetry package outside the chart. Provider teardown shares one wall clock deadline, and supervised worker restarts have bounded restart and give up outcomes. For chart managed sandboxes with NetworkPolicy enabled, a configured external collector endpoint requires declared runner egress CIDRs; chart rendering refuses an undeclared route. Disabling telemetry requires no collector egress rule. Generation spans now carry redacted, clipped langfuse.observation input and output: input is a prompt length placeholder or the names of tool results, and tool arguments and results are never recorded. A turn scope usage fallback stamps the result total when no generation received per message usage. The collector runs at the platform priority class. Metrics export selects cumulative temporality by default for Prometheus retention; an explicit preference can select delta for supported instruments. The example stale accepted-turn alert aggregates to one alert per installation rather than one per turn.

nodes.label: Langfuse
nodes.subtitle: Traces · metrics · eval scores
nodes.description: The current trace and eval store. The shipping Helm surface pins the reviewed Langfuse web and worker migration set together with ClickHouse 25.12.11.4, avoiding an upstream-republished minor alias; its AVX preflight fails the default installation on AVX-less nodes rather than allowing a migration-incompatible store. Compose retains its separate SSE4.2-safe ClickHouse pin for local evidence. The API reconstructs trees and metrics through a vendor-specific read adapter. Operators can disable the in-chart deployment and point every consumer at an explicit external Langfuse host without rendering a nonexistent in-cluster Service. External Langfuse and ClickHouse endpoints use validated HTTP or HTTPS scheme settings shared by their chart consumers. Observation trees expose toolName from the recorded tool span attribute so a consumer can identify the concrete tool executed. Langfuse web and worker now run at the platform priority class so sandboxes cannot preempt the trace store.

nodes.label: Postgres
nodes.subtitle: Control-plane state
nodes.description: Stores agents, versions, deployments, channel bindings, approvals, memory, WorkItems, ExecutionRequests, hook runs, factory status and outcome state, and per thread transcripts. Migrations 0040 through 0056 add scoped publication and review authority, operator source bindings, factory admission and dispatch, cron slots, publication policy, tenant groundwork, isolated transcripts, cancellation, execution deadlines, and status comments. Database constraints and compare and set versions fence competing publication, review, and factory work. Migration 0058 widens the factory terminal notice label check to accept the curie-factory names while retaining the legacy names, so a stored legacy label drives the next GitHub relabel. Migrations 0059 through 0061 record observed publication metadata, reconcile and remove legacy transcript state rows, and store canonical arguments for approved permission calls. After 0060 the transcript table is the sole runtime transcript store. Migrations 0062 through 0070 add durable review notices, factory revision queues, runner resources, deferred schedule claims and controls, model usage, caller allowlists, and identity scoped channel routes. Migrations 0075 and 0076 add durable source policies and immutable source-operation attempts. Candidate application serving metadata and ordered ancestry are owned by packages/protected-hooks, with checked API and chart mirrors. The candidate serving head is 0093 and minimum is 0076; historical released windows remain separately recorded. Migrations 0079, 0080 and 0081 add hook reasons, hook source separation and the nullable reviewer model override. Migrations 0091 through 0093 add the owner-loss successor marker, start-deferral count and versioned factory status-sync lease. The v0.12.3 window is 0076 through 0093.

nodes.label: RustFS / S3
nodes.subtitle: Immutable bundles
nodes.description: Stores immutable agent bundles, eval inputs, managed workspaces, and inbound attachment bytes over an S3 compatible service. The API ObjectStore, worker BundleReader, and worker WorkspaceObjectPort are three distinct adapter surfaces. Attachment materialization additionally requires streaming operations and presigned reads. With a bring your own store and egress rail enabled, runner bundle fetch is fail closed until explicit store CIDRs and ports are supplied; the key free path also requires separate STS egress and uses projected service account identity rather than node metadata.

nodes.label: Kubernetes
nodes.subtitle: Production substrate
nodes.description: Baseline production substrate: platform services, Agent Sandbox CRDs, security rails, connector workloads, and observability dependencies. A canonical external values profile disables the four chart owned backing stores and points consumers at operator supplied endpoints and Secrets. Helm upgrades preserve external credential references and heal missing or blank legacy chart managed Secret keys while retaining nonblank persisted values. Explicit adoption records a separate label pair and is retained on teardown. Runner API and OTLP egress rails key from the effective endpoint, including extra environment overrides, and fail closed without narrow peers. Connector and general runner egress entries require concrete ports and refuse metadata covering ranges or ineffective exceptions. Mail's external collector path has the same explicit peer requirement. In fake mode the worker and runner receive no live model credential, and an inference weights PVC with the keep annotation survives removal of the local model workload. Chart rendering rejects duplicate reserved environment variables; upgrade drains and digest pinned prewarm bundle fetch images are tied to the candidate generation, and BYO Postgres security probes omit an in chart endpoint they cannot reach. The platform PriorityClass now also covers Langfuse, the OTel collector, the UI, inference, and the mail adapter, while runner prewarm stays unclassed. Per agent registry egress policies pass the same floor as connector egress, and the worker Role gains namespaced get on pods for unschedulable diagnosis. The controller preflight rejects current forbidden-NetworkPolicy logs first. An unchanged controller can pass from complete rollout, a current ready leader held beyond the cache-sync bound, and an observed advancing Lease renewal. Earlier restart history does not override that current stable-leader proof. Other startup paths still require startup logs or successful reconciles and reject current failure signals.

nodes.label: Docker
nodes.subtitle: Local parity substrate
nodes.description: Runs the same worker and runner image locally behind the same SandboxClient contract. Connector secret claims bypass Kubernetes pool validation because Docker forwards the declared values to its runner.

nodes.label: Dark Factory
nodes.subtitle: Operating pattern
nodes.description: A shipped single agent bundle and durable platform loop for one labelled GitHub issue and one pull request. Signed issue intake admits a WorkItem, SQL owns waiting and execution identity, the worker claims an isolated sandbox, and an explicitly configured automatic publication policy can open or revise the same pull request. Status comments, cancellation, worker loss recovery, bounded three hour runs, CI wait and repair rounds, and outcome reads are part of this operating pattern. The platform records state and evidence; the bundle owns correctness judgments. Factory state labels use the curie-factory prefix, and a label whose webhook was lost is admitted by reconciliation. The CI wait defaults to 1200 seconds as an operator setting under the execution deadline, the platform reports the wait_ci phase, repair prompts include bounded Actions job log tails, and a configured card URL replaces the checklist. An unpublished execute turn gets one continuation and zero work ends as early_stop; SDK USD budget stops map to the budget failure, and unschedulable sandboxes defer for capacity. Covered turns carry a scoped publication precheck so an empty publication request is refused inside the turn. Publication can revise pull request title or body without a new source commit when the bound identity and CI evidence remain current. Human review events arriving before the pull request identity is recorded are held for bounded admission replay. Verified review mentions received during an active run remain durable queued requests and are admitted after that run. Factory runs now report measured usage and can use a bundle layered runner image. An accepted test policy permits an isolated end to end namespace on a separate test cluster. The bundle reads its issue and comments through mcp__curie__get_issue without a GitHub credential in the sandbox. Foreground plan and diff reviews are enforced, canonical verification observations gate publication, and one Actions rerun on the exact current head precedes bounded repair. Releases publish the first party factory runner layer, and rendering records digest locks for both that layer and its platform runner base. Polling is the default intake and uses durable cursors under a replica lock. Each admitted ticket retains its selected base branch through execution and publication. The first test environment connector provides owned namespace creation and destruction with quotas, expiry and network restrictions; image building, workload deployment, execution and reaping are not established by that slice. Repository edits require the loaded workflow and an approved plan. Declared unavailable verification without explicit CI delegation stops the run before model execution. Delegated check names must be observed and pass before CI settlement; unrelated passing checks cannot substitute. Reviewer credit refusal ends the turn. Accounting separates implementer and reviewer measurements and distinguishes zero usage from missing reports. Provider subscription usage refusals have a distinct terminal model-usage-limited classification, take precedence over credit refusals and interrupt before SDK retries or parent continuation. An OpenRouter key spend-limit 403 remains credit exhaustion. Budget accounting counts a repeated assistant response id once per turn. Factory usage pairs base model observations with a unique context-window-suffixed aggregate key and avoids counting already reported reviewer usage twice; API pricing strips the trailing context suffix before matching rates. When head checks fail, factory CI reads the current base branch head within the remaining observation budget. Matching failing check names or status contexts are reported as pre-existing and excluded from repair, but required Python or delegated checks failing on that base remain unverified. An unreadable base makes every head failure count as caused. A refused factory publication snapshot ends with approval_create_failed and carries the existing redacted, clipped refusal detail into the issue Details line. A sanitized-base mismatch names the first 12 hexadecimal characters of both snapshot and prepared commits; repository mismatch wording and refusal behavior remain unchanged. Publication prose reports CI at pull request creation time and points to the issue status comment for subsequent results. An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries. Factory status synchronization owns a versioned SQL lease, releases database sessions before GitHub I/O, and runs separately from dispatch reconciliation. Late matching runtime heartbeats may renew before the execution deadline, with one heartbeat-TTL grace before owner-loss cancellation. Verification replay preserves the first observation for an unchanged command. CI reports unavailable required check names and merge_conflict explicitly instead of waiting for checks GitHub will not start. Publication snapshots accumulate the response through EOF under the encoded and decoded size limits. Retryable read faults receive at most three reads within the remaining budget, without rerunning the model. Exhaustion names infrastructure read failure in the issue. Idempotent publication creation and execution settlement writes retry transient API faults within bounded authority; unresolved terminal reports retain heartbeat and sandbox ownership until settlement or the execution deadline. Charged publication reconciliation retries back off from fifteen seconds to five minutes. Default factory reviewer selections were updated; per-agent overrides remain explicit. Adoption of an orphaned factory PR under accepted ADR 0208 and post-drain pause handoff under accepted ADR 0209 remain planned for later implementation.

nodes.label: Chief of Staff
nodes.subtitle: Operating pattern
nodes.description: A scheduled briefing pattern that reads across sources on a fixed cadence and posts one digest to a channel. It is a bundle plus a schedule plus a channel binding, not a new architecture box.

nodes.label: SRE triage
nodes.subtitle: Example bundle
nodes.description: A shipped example bundle that triages alerts, gathers Kubernetes evidence, and gates mutations through approval routes. Its default credential limits writes to demo workloads. An optional, operator applied grant expands that same connector across built in resources while keeping Secret reads blocked; approval remains the checkpoint for writes, but the connector credential itself carries the wider Kubernetes authority. This is a bundle policy choice within the isolated runtime. Its reliability alerts count a new counter series' first sample and watch always recorded gauges for absent metrics, and the acceptance path provisions its observability connector before the first deploy. The installer can add observability to an existing release without upgrading Curie. It selects Alloy parsing from the uniform eligible node runtime and refuses mixed or unsupported formats. Reliability alerts observe active log files, stopped Loki delivery, and missing Alloy scrapes.

nodes.label: Agent identity
nodes.subtitle: Who the agent is
nodes.description: The agent record and its principal: the name a channel binds to, the credentials it may use, and the approval routes that answer for it. Identity is what Curie supplies to an agent that was authored anywhere else. Accepted ADR-0155 fixes the future tenant, human principal, provider installation, bot identity, release, and installation vocabulary, Its tenant schema groundwork has landed, while the broader identity and enforcement stages remain incomplete. An installation now selects among declared Slack bot identities. Each identity has its own application token and binding route; the dispatcher and reply path preserve that selection through a turn. A binding may also restrict which callers can reach its bot.

nodes.label: Agent bundle
nodes.subtitle: What it knows
nodes.description: The versioned bundle that carries the agent prompt, skills, tool policy, and connector declarations. It is the unit that moves between installs.

nodes.label: Agent deployment
nodes.subtitle: Where it runs
nodes.description: The active deployment of a bundle in one install: the sandbox template, the substrate it claims, and the channel it answers on. Replacing the deployment is how an agent is upgraded. A deployment can select a bundle supplied runner image layered on the platform base, with admission and resource settings checked before its sandbox starts.

seams.label: Channel ingress + binding
seams.implementations: 3 shipped channel adapters (Slack Bolt, Discord HTTP, email HTTP with current inbound admission refused), a built-in cluster-message reply relay, plus the CLI transport stub
seams.contract: QueuedTurn + ReplyHandle; neutral {kind, address} deployment binding; adapter scoped Attachment references accepted by TurnIn and resolved at the binding endpoint
seams.reason: Slack, Discord, and email all mint or consume the same channel neutral QueuedTurn and (kind, address) binding. Discord and email prove the HTTP edge that Slack does not use, every adapter token remint rotates its row generation, and the reserved built-in cluster-message relay provides the third ReplySink implementation for CLI-driven turns. Slack additionally proves that file references can cross ingress without putting bytes or URLs on the wire. Bindings can limit their admitted caller set, and Slack turns retain the selected bot identity. TurnIn now carries references onto the queue, and the worker selects SlackFileClient or ChannelPortFileClient by binding kind. The generic client fetches opaque ids from the binding endpoint with the same adapter egress credential used for reply delivery. In the cluster relay, adapter chooses reply delivery while optional ReplyHandle.identity chooses the named Slack binding; unknown identities refuse. Named hook signatures use curie.hook.delivery.v2 and authenticate the requested tool_access policy. The email HTTP implementation remains shipped, but current AgentMail messages are refused before the HTTP ingress call because sender authentication is unverifiable. The interface now documents the signed hook tool-access path.
seams.leakage: Discord v1 and email do not share Slack's in process dispatcher or approval cards; exact address validation remains Slack specific while other kinds use the generic nonempty rule. Discord and mail still emit no attachment references, so their attachment producer behavior remains unproved despite the shipped generic transport. A read only hook receipt cannot establish homogeneous worker and runner support.
