seams.nextStep: Exercise another channel attachment producer against the shipped generic transport and establish verifiable sender authentication before reopening email intake.

seams.label: Reply delivery semantics
seams.implementations: 4 ReplySink implementations (Slack, HTTP reply wire used by Discord and email, built-in cluster-message relay, acknowledge-only GitHub)
seams.contract: ReplySink.emit over turn.status, reply.update, reply.post, and turn.completed
seams.reason: The four versioned reply events now leave the worker for three surfaces. Slack still owns edit-in-place streaming and approval-card settlement. The reply wire defines stable progress delivery identities. Scoped API ingress now reaches the durable worker progress store, while progress rendering and adapter delivery remain disabled. The cluster message reply relay retains its reserved adapter after channel binding. Terminal action receipts follow the installation setting.
seams.leakage: Discord v1 falls back to text and does not implement buttons. Email sends one correspondent-visible reply per turn.completed and resolves approvals through scoped reply references rather than interactive buttons. Neither surface may fall back to Slack. The kernel also asks undeliverable_reason and edits_in_place through undeclared capability methods. ReplySinkRouter supplies silent defaults for implementations lacking them, so another identity-aware or edit-capable adapter receives no protocol conformance failure.
seams.nextStep: Keep the HTTP reply wire; add Discord interaction or treat email's one-shot reply as a distinct delivery policy rather than a missing Slack feature.

seams.label: Semantic channel interaction
seams.implementations: 4 renderers (Slack Block Kit, terminal selector, mail approval-card and reply text, Discord plain text)
seams.contract: Versioned OutboundMessage with text fallback, Choice, Confirm, and semantic action values
seams.reason: Slack Block Kit, the terminal selector, mail and Discord consume the shared semantic message with different affordances. Scoped progress ingestion reaches the durable worker store, but rendering remains disabled and no deliverer emits those messages.
seams.leakage: The terminal mirror is handwritten; Rust and Python tests share a schema corpus that gates represented bounds but does not regenerate the Rust model and capabilities are modeled but not dynamically negotiated. Discord renders text without interaction widgets. Mail renders Confirm approval cards and settlement, but current inbound provider replies are refused before resolution; it does not render Choice widgets and drops progress.
seams.nextStep: Wire capability negotiation when a shipped surface other than Slack needs buttons or cards.

seams.label: Queue / stream broker
seams.implementations: 1 real broker (Valkey) behind producer and consumer ports
seams.contract: StreamPublisher + StreamBroker ports, frozen payload field, shared bounded consumer, one renewable fenced owner per delivery, and an independently retried terminal completion outbox; durable generation fenced interactive capacity wait with a fixed deadline and reconciled wake
seams.reason: The port and consumer invariants are explicit, but a second broker has not exercised them. The capacity wait is backed by Valkey atomic scripts, so it does not establish another broker implementation. Protected metadata ACLs, authenticated transport and atomic admission are separate internal Valkey primitives, without a wired protected runtime consumer. They do not establish a second broker implementation. Delivery and consumer liveness renewals tolerate transport errors only until the last confirmed send plus TTL minus one heartbeat interval. A refused renewal loses authority immediately. Side-effect markers retry before applying the frame, and terminal settlement remains fenced. Runs and evals share this ownership rule.
seams.leakage: Some API producers and graveyard readers still bypass the ports; the completion outbox is another off-port writer to the shared graveyard. Conversation lock ownership, liveness records, token checked Lua, set verbs, and redis-py exception types also leak Valkey semantics. Settled retention reads group and pending state and trims with raw Lua outside StreamBroker. DeliveryLeaseStore also reads exact entries and moves pending ownership with XCLAIM JUSTID outside that port.
seams.nextStep: No speculative adapter; promote only if a real broker demand appears.

seams.label: Sandbox substrate
seams.implementations: 2 real implementations (Kubernetes, Docker)
seams.contract: Nine method SandboxClient lifecycle with bounded request deadlines, complete quota rejection evidence, quota_has_headroom, pod_unschedulable, and pod_termination
seams.reason: The same kernel and runner operate through two materially different runtime implementations. Deployments can use a validated layered runner image with per agent resource settings. Every newly created claim receives a fresh boot credential id, preventing replacement or retry claims from reusing a released credential while preserving agent, scope and expiry. Transient Kubernetes reads are treated as no observation while claims bind; on Kubernetes, claim-timeout diagnostics include a bounded redacted runner log tail. A deleted, deletion-marked, or same-name replaced runner pod now classifies as sandbox-terminated, and WorkItem release deletes only the run's own recorded claim.
seams.leakage: SandboxView.port, model credential forwarding, connector secret delivery, warm pool behavior, attachment redemption, and production capacity still differ across Kubernetes and Docker. Docker redeems and bind mounts accepted files in the substrate driver; Kubernetes gives the signed reference only to an init container and keeps it off the runner. Kubernetes proves exact named ResourceQuota headroom before one requester retry; Docker cannot prove Kubernetes quota state and returns false. Retained attachment replacement temporarily needs capacity for two claims. Only Kubernetes can report an Unschedulable pod; Docker returns None. Per agent registry egress and its labeled pool are Kubernetes chart features. Kubernetes rejects a connector secret claim when the rendered agent pool cannot deliver it; Docker has no warm pool and injects the value into the runner directly. Only Kubernetes can confirm termination of the exact claimed pod through status or a matching recent event after the stream began; pod_termination distinguishes sandbox-terminated from a transport failure. Docker returns None for that evidence. Under quota pressure the shared worker reclaims idle eval routes before person routes and attempts idle reclamation for approval resume before a capacity refusal, within the same evidence and deadline bounds. Pool selection branches on the concrete Docker client, while a Kubernetes-only warm_pool_exists probe is undeclared on SandboxClient; a third substrate would inherit these assumptions. Claim-timeout diagnosis bypasses the port: SandboxSubstrate checks for KubernetesSandboxClient and calls its concrete pod_log_tail, which SandboxClient does not declare, so Docker and any third substrate receive no equivalent diagnosis.
seams.nextStep: Keep parity tests focused on the shared outcomes; do not turn substrate choice into a product axis.

seams.label: Cluster lifecycle admission
seams.implementations: 1 Helm and kubectl lifecycle coordinated by the Rust CLI with a worker pre-upgrade hook
seams.contract: Resolve and pin target chart; validate target version, configuration, and schema metadata; own one namespaced CAS checkpoint; drain, migrate once, apply, converge, canary, and commit observed known-good state
seams.reason: The resumable nine-phase driver now owns one namespaced ConfigMap through resourceVersion and holder tests while the pre-upgrade hook keeps installation-scoped drain authority. Retained configuration preserves scalar types and literal dotted keys, explicit context selection binds all child processes to one cluster, and the v0.11.2 release catalog and target API both declare schema 0070 through 0070 independently of the development head. Pending approvals have a versioned additive v2.2 identity shape plus an audited opt-in recovery path for upgrades that strand old rows. The drain gate now holds the quiesce marker as a short renewed lease and caps the post drain roll hold at the drain wait, and status reports the remaining pause. A same version verification records skipped drain, migration, and apply phases distinctly from completed work. The driver checks the rendered drain budget against the Helm timeout before mutation. Caller key checksums roll API and worker. Dev defaults provide a published pair only when neither inline half is present; leaving dev defaults with the retained published key and no replacement refuses. Cluster up preserves recorded runner values and credential references, reuses only a healthy matching unowned controller, and reads the rendered RuntimeClass before the first Helm install. NotFound inference remains distinct from Forbidden admission retry. The historical v0.12.1 serving window is 0076 through 0076. Cluster upgrade removes cleared runner image keys from retained values instead of emitting a null override. Cluster teardown bounds owned namespace deletion to 300 seconds, preserves finalizers, and reports remaining phase, conditions, objects and an exact resume command. A remaining owned namespace yields a transient failure unless an independent permanent teardown failure takes precedence. The controller preflight rejects current forbidden-NetworkPolicy logs first. An unchanged controller can pass from complete rollout, a current ready leader held beyond the cache-sync bound, and an observed advancing Lease renewal. Earlier restart history does not override that current stable-leader proof. Other startup paths still require startup logs or successful reconciles and reject current failure signals. The v0.12.2 serving window is 0076 through 0081. The v0.12.3 target serves 0076 through 0093. Accepted ADR 0209 specifies a live upgrade-step pause lease after drain; the schema-migrate hook now renews that pause while migrating, but the post-drain handoff to it remains planned, while the current clean-drain roll hold remains unchanged. Rollback dry runs select the serving revision from Helm history. Upgrade --take-over lets an operator who has verified that the exact named holder's CLI and Helm action stopped take over its checkpoint; the CLI checks the holder name and refuses while a release hook Job runs. After apply, upgrade retires claims whose runner image differs from the agent's rendered template or cannot be resolved, falling back to agent-wide deletion when the template, claims, or pods cannot be read, and rebinds the stock dark factory layer to the layer published for the target when its base matches.
seams.leakage: Helm, kubectl, rendered chart metadata, worker drain state, approval identity migration fences, and the target API's serving window remain concrete dependencies. The checkpoint is a durable recovery owner, not a general distributed transaction across Helm and Kubernetes. Upgrade refuses absent or partial caller credential pairs before mutation, including dry run, same version verification, and resume. Cluster up can generate a missing pair; upgrade does not. Existing proxies move to replacement keys on agent redeploy or enabled reconciliation, and existing Secret contents changed in place require a manual rollout.
seams.nextStep: Use release upgrade and interruption drills to harden recovery without adding a second lifecycle implementation prematurely.

seams.label: Frozen ACI protocol
seams.implementations: 1 production producer + scripted reference/conformance implementation
seams.contract: SessionConfig, boot env, HTTP control verbs, versioned NDJSON events, optional publication context, canonical approval argument carriers, exact turn admission, and optional per turn tool_access=read-only under ACI 0.5.9, shared across Python, TypeScript, and Rust. Current ACI 0.5.15 also carries the optional BootEnv issue read route and execution scoped capability, plus per turn memory write authority. ACI 0.5.15 adds optional BootEnv.reviewer_model, forwarded as CURIE_REVIEWER_MODEL. Local and cluster overrides can pin or clear it. Ordinary and eval boots forward the per-agent value; omission preserves the override and explicit null clears it. Without an override the runner resolves the SDK Opus alias from the effective credential. Factory quickstart selects a provider-appropriate implementer default for Anthropic or OpenRouter credentials while preserving an explicit model.

The additive publication context carries a signed execution scoped capability for covered factory turns; its absence preserves the existing path for other producers. Approval grants now bind the resumed call to the stored JSON argument object, including an empty object, and the runner admits only the waiting epoch before it receives the turn input. For a restricted turn, the worker checks the exact runner's advertised enforcement before dispatch. The runner denies tools outside its read only set before approvals or registered callbacks, including tools that require approval even if otherwise classified read only. Restricted steers and slash commands refuse. A session that already sent an unrestricted prompt cannot accept a restricted one; the first unrestricted prompt after a restricted one replaces the SDK session. The worker binds factory issue read authority, and the runner mounts the platform issue tool only when both boot fields are present. The serving runner now refuses a missing bearer credential unless explicit development tokenless serving is enabled. Per-turn memory credentials reach the runner process inside the sandbox, while remaining absent from boot environment and hook or subprocess input.
seams.leakage: A non-Claude harness must still consume or translate the Claude Code plugin bundle shape. A producer must establish compatible worker and runner artifacts; a hook receipt proves queued policy rather than homogeneous fleet enforcement.
seams.nextStep: Use the conformance guide against a genuinely different production harness.

seams.implementations: 1 production SDK, fake session, and offline blocked-preflight session
seams.contract: In-process ModelSession protocol and declared harness contribution
seams.reason: The named protocol is real, but its message union is still SDK-shaped and the bundle distribution format is Claude Code verbatim. PreflightBlockedSession provides an offline zero-token failure response for blocked declared verification; it is not a second production harness.
seams.leakage: A foreign harness must emit Claude SDK-shaped objects or replace the runner adapter while also interpreting the Claude plugin format. Read-only enforcement is implemented in SDK callback fronts rather than a ModelSession operation. A foreign harness must enforce it itself or the runner can advertise a restriction the harness does not apply.
seams.nextStep: Prove the out-of-process ACI boundary with a second harness; keep provider-native checkpointing an optional capability.

seams.contract: HarnessContribution manifest; built-ins resolve directly and third-party contributions use curie.harness entry points
seams.reason: Selection and declared assets are clean, but there is no second real package and third-party conformance remains unproven.

seams.implementations: Multiple live endpoints through one Claude-SDK / Anthropic-wire strategy

Local and cluster overrides can pin or clear it. Ordinary and eval boots forward the per-agent value; omission preserves the override and explicit null clears it. seams.reason: Several endpoints exercise routing and credential resolution, but they do not represent multiple independent provider or harness implementations of the boundary. Provider subscription usage refusals have a distinct terminal model-usage-limited classification, take precedence over credit refusals and interrupt before SDK retries or parent continuation. An OpenRouter key spend-limit 403 remains credit exhaustion. Budget accounting counts a repeated assistant response id once per turn. Factory usage pairs base model observations with a unique context-window-suffixed aggregate key and avoids counting already reported reviewer usage twice; API pricing strips the trailing context suffix before matching rates.

seams.nextStep: Add native OpenAI wire only when its semantics are tested through the live-provider parity tier.

seams.label: Telemetry / OTLP
seams.implementations: 1 trace backend (Langfuse) behind an OTel collector
seams.contract: OTLP write path + versioned phase semantics + Curie API DTO read path
seams.reason: Curie preserves valid W3C parentage from ingress through durable approval resolution, expiry, and reconciliation. Request path operation spans may carry a task local channel event id without widening metric cardinality. The runner records real provider and tool intervals, Discord uses the shared bootstrap, chart CI discovers instrumented workloads, provider shutdown shares one deadline, and supervised restarts emit bounded restart and give up outcomes. Only Langfuse has exercised both sides. A transcript over its per-thread cap produces a bounded value-limit failure counter, and observation trees preserve concrete tool identity. Generation spans now record redacted input placeholders and output with a turn scope usage fallback. The shared metrics bootstrap defaults to cumulative export for Prometheus and permits an explicit temporality preference for supported instruments. Factory execution now reports measured usage through runner and API records. Provider subscription usage refusals have a distinct terminal model-usage-limited classification, take precedence over credit refusals and interrupt before SDK retries or parent continuation. An OpenRouter key spend-limit 403 remains credit exhaustion. Budget accounting counts a repeated assistant response id once per turn. Factory usage pairs base model observations with a unique context-window-suffixed aggregate key and avoids counting already reported reviewer usage twice; API pricing strips the trailing context suffix before matching rates. Operators can add ordered extra trace processors between memory_limiter and batch. An SDK server error naming a transport failure is classified as retryable model-unreachable.
seams.leakage: Vendor attributes and /langfuse URL namespaces still leak into the otherwise neutral boundary; the read adapter spans multiple modules. The default collector trace pipeline has no attribute mapping, and optional trace processors are operator configuration rather than a shipped mapping. Generation content is written under langfuse.observation attribute names, adding vendor naming on the write side.
seams.nextStep: Ship a default collector mapping for vendor span attributes and neutralize read-route naming.

seams.label: Eval case + scorer
seams.implementations: Multiple grader kinds plus a trajectory matcher across Python and Rust
seams.contract: Frozen eval-case schema + shared trajectory vectors + tri-state outcomes
seams.reason: Distinct scoring implementations and two languages exercise the case boundary, with shared fixtures pinning semantics.
seams.leakage: Python and Rust still implement graders separately; cluster answer-quality failure is not yet universally fatal.
seams.nextStep: Land semantic provenance verification before making cluster answer-quality promotion fatal.

seams.label: Eval result store
seams.implementations: 1 backend (Langfuse traces + scores)
seams.contract: Eval recorder write + EvalMatrix read DTO + version:/suite: tag convention
seams.reason: The platform owns the result shape, but only one backend and one unfrozen tag convention have exercised it.
seams.leakage: The recorder and matrix reader encode Langfuse tags and API behavior directly.
seams.nextStep: Record or freeze the tag convention; wait for a real second store before inventing a generic adapter.

seams.label: Blob storage
seams.implementations: 1 backend (RustFS) over S3-compatible protocol
seams.contract: API ObjectStore + worker BundleReader + worker WorkspaceObjectPort + bundle, attachment, and managed workspace init paths A text-only follow-up can hand a fresh sandbox the newest retained attachment set for the same thread and agent. The worker remints short-lived object references without extending retention; missing, near-expiry or malformed sets are omitted, and the best-effort lookup is bounded to five seconds.
seams.reason: The port is explicit and S3-compatible services are configuration swaps, but no non-S3 implementation has tested the abstraction.
seams.leakage: API and worker use three separate adapter surfaces. Workspace and attachment operations additionally require streaming put and get, delete, list, and presigned reads. Bucket bootstrap, init containers, migration, key free auth, and NetworkPolicy CIDR configuration retain S3 specific obligations.
seams.nextStep: Leave it alone until a real non-S3 demand appears; keep the BYO egress and web-identity render assertions as the fail-closed operational boundary.

seams.label: Relational database
seams.implementations: 1 engine family (Postgres; self-hosted or managed)
seams.contract: SQLAlchemy models + Alembic migrations + DSN, including scoped workspace identity, fenced pull request lineage, immutable GitHub identity, revision reservations, review audit, adapter principal audit, and durable outbox rows Source policies and immutable operation history add generation-fenced administration.
seams.reason: Managed Postgres is a clean operational swap, but another SQL engine has not exercised the model boundary. The candidate API serving head is 0093 and minimum is 0076, sourced from the protected-hooks package and mirrored into API and chart metadata. Read-only startup probes verify one live revision and readable source-policy and operation columns with compatible types; this proves structure, not runtime qualification. Historical release windows remain separate. Migrations 0079, 0080 and 0081 add hook reasons, hook source separation and the nullable reviewer model override. Migrations 0091 through 0093 add the owner-loss successor marker, start-deferral count and versioned factory status-sync lease. The v0.12.3 window is 0076 through 0093.
seams.leakage: Postgres UUID, JSONB, schema qualification, native enums, DISTINCT ON SQL, asyncpg-specific JSONB decoding, PostgreSQL 15 NULLS NOT DISTINCT workflow-state identity, partial unique indexes for active publication ownership, and database constraints for one active lineage and reservation ownership remain in application code or migrations. Session and transaction advisory locks, the separate int4 and bigint lock spaces, and NULLS NOT DISTINCT constraints for bindings and transcripts also require preserving Postgres-specific semantics.
seams.nextStep: Keep Postgres opinionated unless a concrete alternate engine demand emerges.

seams.label: Approval authorizer
seams.implementations: 5 approver sets (Slack channel, Slack user group, explicit users, email list, no verifiable approvers)
seams.contract: ApproverSet / ApprovalCreator + authenticated ApprovalPrincipal + durable semantic approval record, with one interactive resolution card, a fresh publication approval for each revision, and a separately granted audited recovery path ; covered factory turns resolve empty publication proposals through one shared runner decision before pending state
seams.reason: Five approver-set implementations exercise one API-owned authorization interface after resolver identity is authenticated separately. Chat, Console, operator, and adapter credentials all derive server-owned principal facts before that common decision. The shipped SRE publication gate carries its policy route, enabling explicit user operator resolution; durable rows precede transport delivery. The recorded request location selects the resolving route, and a settled card remains a decision record. Factory publication additionally requires canonical verification observations without changing principal eligibility. Email membership and card authorization remain implemented, while current AgentMail replies are refused before resolution because their sender authentication is unverifiable.
seams.leakage: Channel membership remains Slack-shaped, while Console, operator, and adapter principals are intentionally eligible for only the approver sets their credential kind can satisfy: operators answer explicit-user sets, adapters answer email lists, and neither answers a Slack set. The administrative recovery route deliberately bypasses ordinary membership only when its installation grant is enabled and writes an atomic audit entry. Publication approvals settle durable publication state rather than resuming a model turn, and optional pager delivery is text only. The ADR 0174 precheck is a factory only, read only comparison with its own ppc capability; ordinary managed publication keeps the existing approval path. Bound title or body changes can be admitted without a source commit when identity and current CI evidence pass.
seams.nextStep: Exercise the scoped adapter principal through another interactive channel before broadening approval authority.

seams.label: Approval principal identity
seams.implementations: 4 authenticated principal kinds (chat, Console, operator, adapter)
seams.contract: Canonical ApprovalPrincipal + credential-kind eligibility + authenticated audit fields
seams.reason: Four independent credential paths derive one server-owned principal shape before the common membership decision. The adapter credential is bound to a subject, a nonempty set of channel bindings, three exact scopes, and a bounded expiry. The authenticated adapter and selected bot identity are checked against the recorded route before resolution. Console API and approval requests now carry the live HttpOnly session rather than a browser-held platform key, with origin checking before cookie-authenticated mutations.
seams.leakage: Chat attestations remain Slack-specific, operator principals are limited to explicit-user sets, adapter principals are eligible only for email-list sets on approvals routed to bindings they serve, with no Slack channel, Slack user group, or explicit-user eligibility, and Console principals cannot assert channel evidence.
seams.nextStep: Exercise the adapter principal with another real interactive channel without widening any existing principal kind or accepting the platform key as resolver identity.

seams.label: Workflow state store
seams.implementations: 1 state API router over Postgres JSONB
seams.contract: Scoped namespace/key document API with size limits, CAS behavior, and singular shared NULL-scope identity
seams.reason: The HTTP state router is useful, but not every state consumer stays behind it; operator memory and relational paths can bypass the supposed boundary. Successful state deletes and operator memory edits and deletes emit content free operation logs and bounded mutation metrics; ordinary state writes record none, and stored values and memory content are excluded. Action completion and undo acquisition are conditional SQL transitions, and redacted action results retain no prior or post snapshot and cannot promise restore. Binding claims now confine sandbox memory and transcript reach; memory fact writes require a live turn credential and cannot overwrite operator guidance. The API refuses released boot credential ids and closed per-turn write claims. A boot release report that fails remains queued for retry; a failed turn-close report leaves that write credential valid until expiry. The operator memory plane also accepts a live Console session. Every newly created claim receives a fresh boot credential id, preventing replacement or retry claims from reusing a released credential while preserving agent, scope and expiry.
seams.leakage: A second state backend would not cover direct model/JSONB access, while memory and transcript loaders still depend on the HTTP shape and capacity limits.
seams.nextStep: Inventory and close bypasses before extracting another backend; then treat retention, capacity, and back-pressure as one admission policy.

seams.label: Agent memory
seams.implementations: 1 loader plus a facts store on the same Postgres backing
seams.contract: Memory loading plus agent and channel fact tools, with binding scoped reads and turn scoped writes
seams.reason: The loader port remains single backed. A separate facts store provides bounded remember, update and forget operations and prompt loading; the API enforces channel scope, fact keys and server recorded authors. Boot reads are claim-scoped with a credential id and bounded expiry, and released ids are refused. Per-turn writes have no expiry grace; steering hands closure ownership to the live turn, while an unsuccessful close remains valid until its deadline. The write token reaches the in-sandbox ACI runner process but stays out of boot environment, hook input and subprocess input. Every newly created claim receives a fresh boot credential id, preventing replacement or retry claims from reusing a released credential while preserving agent, scope and expiry.
seams.leakage: The operator inspect/seed/edit/delete plane addresses the Postgres WorkflowStateEntry backing directly instead of going through MemoryStore. Legacy SessionRunner.remember appends and consolidation replacement PUTs need platform authorization; the worker's boot token and per-turn fact credentials cannot write the legacy log, so in-sandbox writes go through the remember fact tool.
seams.nextStep: Keep loader, facts and operator paths consistent; automatic compaction remains separate work.

seams.label: Conversation history
seams.implementations: 1 real loader (StateApiTranscriptStore)
seams.contract: TranscriptStore load/append of portable structured turn and summary records, scoped by agent and thread
seams.reason: One real state API store supports structured replay, tool result continuity, bounded compaction, optional native checkpoint reuse, and versioned capacity recovery. Appends reserve space for publication outcomes; on 413 the store rewrites a compacted value by compare-and-set, preserves publication markers and the newest turn, reloads on conflict, and retries before returning a classified terminal failure. The state API advertises its transcript value cap and the runner requires it for every bound, and a single long turn can replace older completed tool exchanges with a deterministic marker while keeping the first user message, final answer, recent pairs, and pending approval. Migration 0060 reconciles newer legacy rows, removes them, and blocks future legacy transcript writes, leaving the transcript table authoritative. Assistant grouping records causal evidence rather than inferring a group from arrival order, and unprovable overlapping tool calls reduce the affected turns to visible user and assistant text, transitively across turns, clearing the native checkpoint; other malformed history is still refused. Subagent messages stay out of portable history while the parent's Agent call and result remain. A boot's attachment notice rides on the first actual prompt and its durable user message, so reattaching the same filename remains visible even when the system prompt matches a native checkpoint.
seams.leakage: Compaction deliberately replaces older message and tool detail with a bounded summary and drops the old native checkpoint. Each thread transcript has its own byte cap with no agent-wide cap, and a value that cannot fit its publication markers, summary, newest turn, and reserve requires operator recovery through versioned export and delete. Ordinary persistence failure marks durability lost, preventing safe cold handoff. A fresh text-only boot currently announces retained thread files as though the current message carried them; the interface records the pending notice correction in #4081.
seams.nextStep: Keep portable replay authoritative, preserve publication outcomes under pressure, and make any future source retention policy explicit.

seams.label: Trigger ingestion
seams.implementations: 8 hardcoded ingress paths (Slack, GitHub push, GitHub review, commit polling, HMAC hooks, factory issue events, factory poll intake, missed-label reconcile) plus worker cron slots
seams.contract: No unified runtime trigger port. Bespoke authenticated producers converge on QueuedTurn and bounded stream delivery; factory issues and reviews retain their durable authority and outbox checks, cron claims one SQL slot, and generic hooks keep HMAC and delivery admission. Signed hooks and ordinary manual or scheduled cron admission also hold current SQL source authority and recheck liveness before effects; configured policy or durable history closes those ordinary paths. hook_runs.source separates manual and scheduled histories, and settlement records a closed vocabulary of terminal reason codes.
seams.reason: Slack, GitHub push and review, factory issues, commit polling, named HMAC hooks, and cron have distinct producer admission rules but converge on the typed queue boundary. Declared cron schedules ship and can be test fired through the operator route without losing their single slot admission. The lost factory label reconciler reuses webhook verification after its grace period. Hook signatures use the curie.hook.delivery.v2 domain and authenticate the requested tool_access policy with the delivery data. Protected source records, signing, broker metadata transport and atomic admission/recovery are internal primitives. Complete protected provisioning, consumer lifecycle and qualified execution remain planned. Protected admission recovery preparation is bounded to 32 attempts. Reads that straddle a concurrent commit are reread before an inconsistent combination is refused; stable orphan combinations remain fail-closed. This does not establish protected consumer wiring or qualified execution.
seams.leakage: Slack enters through dispatcher; GitHub push, review, factory issues, polling, and generic hooks enter through API handlers; cron starts in the worker. Review feedback and factory work have their own durable admission and outbox rules. Bundle declared generic hook installation remains planned. Missed factory label recovery polls GitHub from the API reconciler rather than a shared trigger lifecycle.
seams.nextStep: Wire bundle declared generic webhooks into deployment and define their delivery destinations and operator admission; preserve the existing producer authority checks and bounded QueuedTurn delivery.

seams.label: Protected hook source authority
seams.implementations: 0 production resolvers; tests inject the only implementation
seams.contract: SourceAuthorityResolver.resolve opens a SourceControlSession for the requested source and target under the agent source gate; its reader returns a reconciled generation floor and its writer reserves and publishes the next generation
seams.reason: SourceMutationCoordinator owns the Postgres policy half and reaches the broker half only through the injected resolver. With no resolver it refuses with source_authority_unavailable before any write, and protected-mode publication is refused even when a resolver is present.
seams.leakage: No production code implements the resolver or constructs the coordinator, so broker endpoint, credential, runtime epoch, and qualification selection are unbuilt.
seams.nextStep: Write the first production resolver against this port when protected hook provisioning is wired; do not add an adapter layer first.

seams.label: Agent-facing CLI output
seams.implementations: 67 typed outputs behind one trait across many verbs, with 65 committed non-baseline schemas
seams.contract: CliOutput + Ui.emit + versioned JSON result schemas. The strict dark factory renderer receipt schema v2 requires bundle_dir, rendered, runner_image, and runner_note. Its runner fields accept string or null and unknown fields are rejected. Hook fire succeeds only for the durable ran outcome; failed, blocked, skipped and reclaimed outcomes fail while preserving the record and reason. Open runs remain polled until settlement or a transient timeout naming the same-tier record command. Hook record reads an existing run without waiting or judging its outcome. Schedule reads separate newest scheduled and manual histories. Deploy schema v1.2 always includes cron declarations and advisory warnings from the immutable uploaded bundle; unresolved explicit targets warn after successful deployment.
seams.reason: Many independent command results exercise the same human/JSON emission boundary.
seams.leakage: A tracked set of legacy/operator verbs still has inline or unstructured success output.
seams.nextStep: Finish migrating the tracked exceptions without widening the output contract.

seams.label: MCP connector host
seams.implementations: 1 real Kubernetes host + in-memory fake
seams.contract: Bundle declaration → rendered workload → bounded rollout readiness → mounted MCP entry → runner capability probe
seams.reason: The lifecycle now observes rollout and runner capability outcomes, and transient probe failures can recover on later turns. The renderer and CLI share frozen vectors for the derived Bearer rule, accepting an explicit bearer_secret or one plain-string secret while excluding an implicit SecretRef. The typed client still exposes raw Kubernetes JSON, rendering remains Kubernetes specific outside the port, and CLI and reconciler paths do not share identical apply and prune semantics. TCP readiness now reflects whether the hosted MCP port accepts a connection. Multiple SecretRef credentials remain upstream pod secrets and do not imply client Bearer authentication. The hosted Kubernetes path requires a caller proxy and public key, with API 422 refusal when absent. Its cct proves only agent and expiry, and its admits decision is separate from the one use, argument bound ccg needed for approval gated calls. The Docker development host requires a public key but runs the original image directly with no caller or grant enforcement.
seams.leakage: Build inputs, pinned images, delegated OAuth, runtime injection, reconciliation, and Kubernetes objects cross control plane and cluster ownership. Only one real host sits behind the port. Skill and local tiers use a separate Docker applier with its own label, pruning, and readiness wait outside this interface. Upgrade refuses absent or partial caller credential pairs before mutation and does not generate a missing pair; cluster up can generate one. Caller key checksums roll API and worker, while existing connector proxies change key only on agent redeploy or enabled reconciliation.
seams.nextStep: Converge CLI and reconciler lifecycle before calling the host portable.

seams.label: MCP service-key authentication
seams.implementations: 1 deployment-owned service identity mode
seams.contract: Named hosted Bearer secret plus a mandatory caller proxy; signed caller claims include agent and expiry with an optional paired run and work item identity; approval grants remain separate
seams.reason: Service credentials cross a named secret boundary, expand into the MCP header in memory, and are removed from the runner process environment before turns, but no second production identity mode has proved the abstraction. For hosted Kubernetes calls, the runner supplies a signed cct with agent and exp, plus an optional paired run and work item identity, and the mandatory proxy checks the admitted agent before forwarding. An approval gated call also needs a separate signed ccg matching agent, connector, tool, canonical args, exp, and jti; Valkey spends that jti once. Docker development connectors run directly without either check.
seams.leakage: Secret rendering and delivery still span bundle declaration, API, Kubernetes, kubelet and container environment exposure before process startup, and SecretRef residuals. With dev defaults and neither inline key half set, the chart supplies a published caller pair. Leaving dev mode with its retained public key and no replacement is refused. A caller checksum rolls API and worker; connector proxies move on redeploy or reconciliation, and an existing Secret rotated in place still needs a manual rollout. The data-tier policy admits connector pods to in-chart Valkey by default; the allowMcpConnectorValkeyIngress opt-out removes only that peer and does not change caller authorization.
seams.nextStep: Keep service authentication explicit and fail closed; prove delegated OAuth as a separate identity mode with no fallback between them.

seams.label: Per-person MCP OAuth
seams.implementations: 0; accepted architecture only
seams.contract: Canonical run principal → principal-scoped grant → control-plane-owned OAuth gateway → MCP server
seams.reason: ADR-0088 defines the ownership and fail-closed behavior, but the gateway, grant lifecycle, connection action, and resume path are not shipped.
seams.leakage: Until implemented, MCP calls cannot safely act with each human's authority; the existing deployment service identity is the only current mode.
seams.nextStep: Implement discovery, PKCE, encrypted grant storage, refresh and revocation, then prove missing-auth pause and post-callback resume without giving the runner a raw token.

seams.label: Sealed connector credential
seams.implementations: 1 cross-language wire (Rust sealer, Python opener)
seams.contract: Frozen sealed-credential envelope with cluster-side opening
seams.reason: The Rust sealer and Python opener interoperate, but the product path is disconnected: validation and delivery do not yet form one working production consumer path.
seams.leakage: Security depends on exact agreement between CLI, API rendering, cluster delivery, and the currently uncalled opener.
seams.nextStep: Connect and prove the complete sealed-secret path before expanding its wire or consumers.

seams.label: Bundle / plugin format
seams.implementations: 1 deliberately adopted format (Claude Code plugin)
seams.contract: Frozen Pydantic models including unhosted_url, SecretRef, and bearer_secret, plus regenerated committed JSON Schema and an immutable content-addressed bundle. The exact platform publication tool mcp__curie__publish_changes is a recognized approval gate without requiring a declared external MCP server. Bundle tool policy cannot remove Curie's built-in platform MCP tools, while a bundle-mounted server named curie remains fully in scope. Invalid cron declarations name the first failing field and distinguish malformed syntax from an out-of-range value. Field-count errors name the existing five-field grammar and observed count. Seven Curie authoring extensions include optionalSecrets. Connector names that forge the -mcp- join are refused only for hosted connectors, those declaring image: or build:; remote url: connectors derive no Kubernetes object name.
seams.reason: The format is strongly enforced but intentionally has one implementation and one ecosystem shape. Bundles can declare a layered runner image and an agent caller policy for hosted connectors. Releases publish the first party factory runner layer, and the renderer records both its layer digest and its platform base digest.
seams.leakage: This is the main coupling that a non-Claude harness must interpret or translate. A published runner lock written by example rendering trusts the release pipeline for the source-to-image link rather than proving it locally.
seams.nextStep: Do not invent another format; require alternate harnesses to demonstrate a translation strategy.

seams.label: Third-party port adapter
seams.implementations: 0 generic adapter-kit services; Discord and email are first-party adapters on the shipped HTTP edge
seams.contract: Intended deployed-service placement with a shipped scoped adapter credential; generic packaging and conformance remain unbuilt
seams.reason: ADR-0096 places a third-party adapter as a deployed service, and ADR-0154 now supplies a scoped runtime principal for channel token rotation plus approval listing and resolution. The generic kit is still unbuilt; first-party Discord and email adapters use the HTTP edge without that kit.
seams.leakage: Adapter discovery, installation, routing, conformance, and lifecycle are still future work. The scoped credential is a prerequisite, not a complete third-party adapter product.
seams.nextStep: Build the adapter kit only if a third-party channel needs install, discovery, and conformance beyond the two shipped first-party adapters.

seams.label: Agent Proxy boundary
seams.contract: Accepted credential and egress enforcement boundary outside the sandbox
seams.reason: The direction is accepted but intentionally unimplemented pending narrower substrate, TLS, and injection decisions.
seams.leakage: Provider credentials and web egress still enter the sandbox under current controls.
seams.nextStep: Land the follow-up ADRs for substrate, TLS termination, and credential injection before implementation.

seams.label: Eval result → promotion authority
seams.implementations: Commit status exists; internal promotion enforcement does not
seams.contract: Reserved policy boundary between graded evidence and production deployment
seams.reason: The API reports eval state to GitHub, but process_push does not read that result before creating a production deployment.
seams.leakage: Safety depends on external branch protection and release policy rather than a product invariant.
seams.nextStep: Land semantic provenance first, then bind promotion to an authoritative graded result without rebuilding the artifact.
