flows.label: Whole system
flows.summary: Every currently visible component and route in one architecture map. Choose a specific flow to isolate and walk its path.

flows.label: Slack turn
flows.summary: A mention and any file references become one queued, isolated, multiturn model session with accepted files mounted read only and one durably delivered edited thread reply. Under capacity pressure an interactive turn is durably queued until an exact runner admission succeeds or its fixed deadline expires. A selected bot identity and caller admission policy are preserved from ingress through reply. A verified bot authored thread root may be quoted as bounded untrusted context with neutralized slashes and no new routing authority.

steps.title: Receive and deduplicate
steps.caption: Bolt receives the mention and file references; the dispatcher claims the event id and posts the placeholder without downloading file bytes. For threaded mentions it verifies a bot authored root and adds bounded untrusted context with neutralized slashes.

steps.title: Normalize ingress
steps.caption: The dispatcher serializes a channel-neutral QueuedTurn onto curie:runs.

steps.title: Claim delivery
steps.caption: The worker consumer group claims the event and acquires the conversation lock.

steps.title: Park accepted attachments
steps.caption: The worker downloads and validates accepted channel references, stores bytes under a private prefix, and mints one short lived signed object reference.

steps.title: Materialize private inputs
steps.caption: A credentialless init path streams, hash verifies, and materializes the immutable bundle and accepted files; the runner receives neither channel nor object store credentials. A text-only follow-up can hand a fresh sandbox the newest retained attachment set for the same thread and agent. The worker remints short-lived object references without extending retention; missing, near-expiry or malformed sets are omitted, and the best-effort lookup is bounded to five seconds.

steps.title: Resolve and isolate
steps.caption: The binding selects agent, version, and bundle, then SandboxClient claims or resumes the runtime with accepted files mounted read only. An idle retained generic thread with files uses a fenced cold replacement only after proving durable history; active or unsafe routes refuse.

steps.title: Start or steer
steps.caption: The worker sends event for a fresh turn or steer for an unrestricted live one. A restricted turn requires the exact runner to advertise enforcement and never steers.

steps.title: Rehydrate durable memory
steps.caption: At boot the runner loads attributed agent and channel facts using its binding scoped read credential before composing the effective prompt. Writes use a separate live turn credential when enabled.

steps.title: Enter the harness
steps.caption: The runner translates the ACI request into the active ModelSession.

steps.title: Run inference
steps.caption: The declared Claude harness calls the selected provider and streams its result.

steps.title: Stream outcomes
steps.caption: The runner emits text deltas, tool notes, side-effect markers, and a terminal result as NDJSON. A transcript capacity refusal replaces a successful or approval final with an explicit classified failure before delivery.

steps.title: Return to the surface
steps.caption: The worker records turn.completed in its durable outbox before the done marker, ReplySink updates the original placeholder, and the stream entry is acknowledged; a failed emit is retried independently.

flows.label: Discord turn
flows.summary: A Discord mention becomes a public thread, a platform-minted QueuedTurn, and streamed text edits on that thread.

steps.title: Admit the mention
steps.caption: adapters/discord creates a public thread and placeholder, then posts to POST /channels/turns under a scoped channel token.

steps.title: Enter the same core
steps.caption: The API mints a channel-neutral QueuedTurn onto curie:runs.

steps.title: Claim delivery
steps.caption: The worker consumer group claims the event under one renewable fenced owner.

steps.title: Resolve and isolate
steps.caption: Multi-surface binding selects the agent by (kind, address) without cloning the bot identity.

steps.title: Start or steer
steps.caption: The worker sends event for a fresh turn or steer for a live one.

steps.title: Return to the thread
steps.caption: HttpReplyAdapter streams text edits to the Discord placeholder. Buttons and approvals are not implemented.

flows.label: Approval + resume
flows.summary: A gated tool call ends the turn, persists authority, suspends the sandbox, then resumes through a new queued event. A permission grant is tied to the denied tool and canonical argument object, and duplicate resume deliveries share one fenced event claim. The request location selects the card route, and settled cards preserve an ordered record in the requester thread.

steps.title: Gate the side effect
steps.caption: The runner terminates AWAITING_APPROVAL; the kernel converts it into durable governance work.

steps.title: Persist the decision point
steps.caption: The API stores the approval, policy, requester, allowed approver set, and validated originating trace context.

steps.title: Render a semantic confirm
steps.caption: Only after the durable row and suspension, the worker delivers the card and pending notice. Missing transport or reply reference does not erase the decision point; operator credentials can resolve routes bound to explicit users.

steps.title: Authorize the human
steps.caption: Slack signs an approval-bound chat attestation; the API derives the principal and resolves membership without trusting caller-supplied identity or channel. A non-owning release acknowledges an exact record miss without changing the approval or card, leaving the owning release's compare-and-set as the only mutation path.

steps.title: Queue a new resolution turn
steps.caption: The original event is already acknowledged; resolution enters as its own QueuedTurn under the stored trace context, while legacy or malformed carriers start clean roots. Failed resume enqueues observed by the current API process are retried on the next reconciler pass. The process record is capped at 10,000 approvals; restart loss and failures beyond that cap retain the grace backstop. A short locked transaction enqueues before marking resumed and retains still-owed locked rows for another pass.

steps.title: Reclaim the conversation
steps.caption: The worker restores the same thread affinity and suspended sandbox.

steps.title: Resume with one-shot allowance
steps.caption: The resolution turn tells the runner whether to continue or terminate the rejected action.

steps.title: Settle the surface
steps.caption: The card becomes non-interactive and the final reply returns to the same conversation.

flows.label: PR / git deploy
flows.summary: A development branch push becomes an immutable bundle, deployment, and eval fan-out; a production push promotes the stored artifact without cloning or rebuilding it.

steps.title: Ingest a push
steps.caption: HMAC webhook or outbound commit poller converges on the same process_push function.

steps.title: Archive, validate, store
steps.caption: The API archives the SHA, validates the frozen plugin shape, and writes an immutable bundle.

steps.title: Create version + deployment
steps.caption: Dev branches activate the new version; production branches promote an existing artifact.

steps.title: Fan out evals
steps.caption: A newly built development bundle appends one deduplicated EvalJob to curie:evals.

steps.title: Grade the exact bundle
steps.caption: The eval consumer loads cases from the immutable bundle and drives the runner.

steps.title: Record evidence
steps.caption: Each case writes a tagged trace; graded cases also write an eval score, while plumbing-only cases remain ungraded.

steps.title: Report the rollup
steps.caption: The worker posts the result to the API.

steps.title: Publish, but do not internally gate
steps.caption: GitHub receives a commit status; production promotion still relies on external policy rather than an API invariant.

flows.label: Eval + parity ladder
flows.summary: One bundle and one case file cross skill, local, local-release, and cluster to expose environment drift.

steps.title: Pin the artifact
steps.caption: Bundle identity fixes the code, tools, and eval cases under test.

steps.title: Load the suite
steps.caption: The worker reads evals/cases.json from that exact immutable bundle.

steps.title: Choose the required tier
steps.caption: Skill, Docker, released Compose, or Kubernetes changes only the substrate rung.

steps.title: Run a fresh case
steps.caption: Each case defaults to a fresh conversation and uses the same ACI loop.

steps.title: Score the outcome
steps.caption: Text graders and trajectory matching produce pass, fail, or plumbing-only.

steps.title: Persist the evidence
steps.caption: Traces, and scores for graded cases, support the matrix and later diagnosis.

flows.label: Observability read/write
flows.summary: Curie preserves valid ingress and approval trace lineage into OTLP; the API turns vendor reads back into Curie DTOs for agents and humans.

steps.title: Emit the run
steps.caption: The runner writes an agent.run root plus real sibling provider-wait and tool-wait intervals, with bounded terminal and outcome attributes, over OTLP.

steps.title: Export once
steps.caption: The collector handles Langfuse authentication and HTTP-only OTLP ingest.

steps.title: Reconstruct the evidence
steps.caption: The API reads traces, builds the tool tree, and proxies metrics and cost.

steps.title: Expose one read surface
steps.caption: Console reads traces, metrics, and cost through Curie API shapes instead of talking to Langfuse directly.

flows.label: MCP with service key
flows.summary: An MCP connector acts as a deployment owned service account. Hosted Kubernetes calls must pass caller admission and, for an approval gated tool, an argument bound one use connector grant. Skill and local Docker connectors run the original image directly without those proxy checks.

steps.title: Reconcile the hosted workload
steps.caption: The worker lists, applies, and deletes the bundle derived Kubernetes connector resources. Hosted rendering requires the caller proxy and public key; the API returns 422 without them.

steps.title: Bind the service identity
steps.caption: The bundle names the connector secret; deployment configuration supplies the value and the platform injects it into the hosted MCP connector.

steps.title: Call the MCP server
steps.caption: The mandatory Kubernetes proxy verifies cct {agent, exp} and admits the agent. An approval gated tool additionally needs a signed ccg matching agent, connector, tool, canonical args, exp, and a jti spent once through Valkey. Transient capability probes may retry on later turns; missing credentials remain terminal. Docker skill and local hosts run directly without caller or grant enforcement, and service credentials remain shared deployment authority.

flows.label: Future per-person MCP OAuth
flows.summary: The accepted vision binds each run's canonical human principal to that person's OAuth grant. Curie applies the grant at a gateway, and the runner never receives the raw token.

steps.title: Resolve principal and grant
steps.caption: The control plane owns OAuth discovery, PKCE, encrypted token storage, refresh, revocation, and the principal-to-grant binding.

steps.title: Call as the run principal
steps.caption: The runner sends a principal-bound MCP request to the gateway without receiving a provider token.

steps.title: Apply delegated authority
steps.caption: The gateway applies only that principal's active grant and exchanges MCP traffic with the declared server. Missing auth pauses the run for a connection action, then resumes after callback.

flows.label: Email turn
flows.summary: Current AgentMail inbound messages are refused before a turn or approval can start because sender authentication is unverifiable. The shipped HTTP and worker path remains available for historical accepted deliveries, whose completion can still send one threaded reply.

steps.title: Refuse unverifiable inbound messages
steps.caption: The adapter polls AgentMail and records authentication_unverifiable in local SQLite before body fetch, HTTP turn admission or approval handling.

steps.title: Retain the historical HTTP path
steps.caption: The adapter retains its row-scoped channel credential and HTTP contract, but current provider messages do not pass the authentication gate and make no POST /channels/turns call.

steps.title: Enter the same core
steps.caption: For historically accepted deliveries, the API minted the same QueuedTurn used by Slack, Discord and the CLI stub. Current provider intake creates no new queued turn.

steps.title: Reuse the worker invariants
steps.caption: Existing accepted work retains ordinary routing, concurrency, sandboxing and renewable delivery ownership.

steps.title: Reuse the ACI
steps.caption: The ACI path remains unchanged for existing accepted work; current provider intake cannot reach model execution.

steps.title: Send one threaded reply
steps.caption: Historical accepted deliveries still receive worker reply events and can send one threaded reply at confirmed completion. Failed terminal delivery remains independently retryable.

flows.label: Generic webhook turn
flows.summary: A named HMAC-authenticated hook becomes a bounded webhook-sourced turn; alert coding targets come only from an operator source binding to an allowlisted repository and recorded revision. Optional tool_access=read-only is queued explicitly; the receipt proves policy, and compatible worker and runner artifacts must enforce it. Signed authentication is repeated under a live source gate; configured policy or operation history refuses this ordinary path. Complete protected delivery remains planned.

steps.title: Authenticate the named hook
steps.caption: The API verifies the per hook HMAC under the curie.hook.delivery.v2 signature domain, authenticates the requested tool_access policy, claims the delivery id, and resolves the target agent. Authentication is repeated under the dedicated SQL source gate, and current configured policy or operation history refuses before claims or enqueue.

steps.title: Apply operator source binding
steps.caption: For a configured alert hook, the API extracts only the named workload field, maps it through operator-owned agent state to an allowlisted repository and recorded revision, and refuses missing, ambiguous, malformed, or unauthorized mappings. Payload URLs never select a workspace.

steps.title: Mint the platform turn
steps.caption: The API creates the typed webhook-sourced QueuedTurn with bounded delivery metadata, escaped and explicitly delimited untrusted payload, and trusted source binding facts outside that payload. A requested read only policy is carried on this exact turn; receipt or replay acknowledgement does not prove fleet enforcement or reply delivery. The held source gate is rechecked before every delivery effect; no protected payload falls back into the ordinary stream.

steps.title: Reuse bounded delivery
steps.caption: The shared consumer claims, caps, and dead-letters the hook turn like other run traffic.

steps.title: Run through the same ACI
steps.caption: The worker drives the selected bundle without a channel adapter in the path. A webhook turn starts fresh and never steers a live session. For a restricted turn it checks the exact runner's advertised enforcement before dispatch; the runner denies disallowed and approval requiring tools before registered callbacks. Restricted slash commands refuse, and incompatible session history cannot accept a restricted prompt.

flows.label: Future bundle hooks
flows.summary: Named HMAC hooks and declared cron schedules ship. Generic bundle declared hook installation beyond these paths remains planned.

steps.title: Reuse API-owned ingress
steps.caption: A future declaration resolves onto the shipped named-hook endpoint rather than a new dispatcher.

steps.title: Create a typed turn
steps.caption: A future declaration must preserve source authority, concurrency, expiry, and bounded delivery when it enters the existing stream.

steps.title: Reuse bounded delivery
steps.caption: The shared stream consumer must still cap attempts, dead-letter, and expose failure.

flows.label: Managed workspace
flows.summary: A scoped server thread selects one allowlisted repository, receives a sanitized private checkout, and can replace a generic sandbox only at a fenced turn boundary.

steps.title: Resolve scoped workspace identity
steps.caption: The worker sends the canonical channel binding plus conversation identity and any trusted repository fact. Review bodies and webhook payload URLs cannot select a repository.

steps.title: Authorize and persist sticky selection
steps.caption: The API derives the agent from durable deployment state, checks the repository allowlist, and atomically establishes or confirms one repository for that scoped thread. A conflicting selection is terminal.

steps.title: Redeem bounded clone authority
steps.caption: The API rechecks current selection and policy, then returns a short lived repository credential for the server-derived target and optional recorded revision only.

steps.title: Clone, sanitize, and archive
steps.caption: The trusted worker clones the selected revision, rewrites and verifies the clean remote, bounds the archive, and stores it under the scoped workspace identity.

steps.title: Materialize the private checkout
steps.caption: A one-object signed reference and digest let credentialless init stream and verify /workspace. The runner receives no GitHub or object store credential.

steps.title: Commit the fenced handoff
steps.caption: A late workspace cold-claims a prepared replacement and compare-and-set swaps the scoped route only at the next turn boundary. A failed or stale candidate leaves the prior route authoritative.

flows.label: Approval gated publication
flows.summary: Each proposed workspace revision receives a fresh durable approval, then a fenced cluster job creates or advances the one pull request owned by that scoped thread and repository. Bound pull request metadata can change without a source commit when identity and CI evidence remain current.

steps.title: Validate the proposed revision
steps.caption: The worker verifies repository, base commit, changed paths, binary patch, scoped workspace identity, and any review reservation before creating governance work. Review feedback never grants publication. Factory publication also validates canonical verification observations before governance work, while ordinary managed publication retains its existing revision authority. Publication snapshots accumulate the response through EOF under the encoded and decoded size limits. Retryable read faults receive at most three reads within the remaining budget, without rerunning the model. Exhaustion names infrastructure read failure in the issue. Idempotent publication creation and execution settlement writes retry transient API faults within bounded authority; unresolved terminal reports retain heartbeat and sandbox ownership until settlement or the execution deadline. Charged publication reconciliation retries back off from fifteen seconds to five minutes.

steps.title: Create approval and publication atomically
steps.caption: One transaction records a fresh revision-bound approval, publication, reply route, immutable lineage authority, and optional review reservation. Stale or already consumed authority is refused. The publication gate carries its declared policy route.

steps.title: Deliver one interactive card
steps.caption: The leased outbox posts the sole interactive resolution card. Any configured pager receives text only and cannot create a second card or approval authority. CLI ingress retains its reply adapter, and card delivery does not shorten the pending approval lifetime.

steps.title: Resolve durable publication authority
steps.caption: An authenticated eligible chat, Console, or operator principal resolves the captured approver set. Denial settles without redeeming a credential or creating a Job; approval never resumes the model.

steps.title: Claim the exact lineage revision
steps.caption: The reconciler leases the approved publication, compare-and-set checks current lineage generation, parent head, reservation, and allowlist, then redeems a short lived writer credential. Terminal or stale lineages are refused.

steps.title: Run a deterministic writer
steps.caption: A tokenless, no-RBAC Job receives the validated patch and file-backed askpass credential, checks out the recorded parent, safely applies and commits, and emits one bounded result marker.

steps.title: Create or advance the same pull request
steps.caption: The fenced branch and lineage generation create the first pull request or advance that same open pull request. Retry adopts the deterministic branch and existing pull request instead of creating a second lineage.

steps.title: Commit lineage and result
steps.caption: The API records the new exact head and parent under compare-and-set, consumes any review reservation, and durably settles the publication result.

steps.title: Settle the original thread
steps.caption: The result outbox updates the card and original scoped reply route exactly once; delivery retry does not rerun repository work.

flows.label: GitHub human review
flows.summary: Human review on the current bound pull request becomes a durable fresh turn in the original scoped thread, starting from the exact accepted head and requiring a new approval before the same pull request advances.

steps.title: Authenticate and normalize feedback
steps.caption: The GitHub route verifies the webhook signature and accepts actionable issue comments, pull request review comments, and submitted reviews into one normalized identity.

steps.title: Verify immutable review authority
steps.caption: Fresh provider reads must match the persisted repository, installation, pull request, binding generation, open state, and exact lineage head. Stale heads and terminal, unavailable, ambiguous, or mismatched authority enqueue no turn.

steps.title: Persist audit and durable outbox
steps.caption: The API commits the delivery receipt, normalized feedback, captured lineage version, original scoped reply route, and outbox row together. Per-lineage reservation serializes distinct feedback without dropping it.

steps.title: Enqueue the original scoped thread
steps.caption: The reconciler appends a typed review turn to the bounded run stream only from durable outbox state; transport retry cannot create a second feedback identity.

steps.title: Claim without steering
steps.caption: The worker recognizes verified review provenance, uses the stored workspace and reply identity, and never treats review text or links as repository selection.

steps.title: Reverify and reserve the exact head
steps.caption: Immediately before work, the worker repeats provider truth checks and compare-and-set reserves a new revision against the captured lineage head. A changed pull request is refused before the model starts.

steps.title: Prepare the accepted pull request head
steps.caption: The trusted workspace path fetches the exact verified head, sanitizes and privately archives it under the scoped identity, rather than reusing an older sandbox checkout.

steps.title: Materialize exact review input
steps.caption: Credentialless init verifies the private workspace digest and mounts the exact pull request head at /workspace.

steps.title: Cold-claim a fenced replacement
steps.caption: The scoped route swaps only after the exact-head candidate is ready; review feedback never steers a live sandbox with stale files.

steps.title: Run the review turn
steps.caption: The reviewer body is untrusted requested-change context, not authority. The runner starts a fresh turn on the accepted head.

steps.title: Require fresh publication approval
steps.caption: If the turn proposes changes, its new revision enters the publication flow and receives a fresh approval before the fenced lineage can advance the same pull request.

flows.label: Cluster lifecycle
flows.summary: Cluster upgrade resolves and validates the exact target chart before mutation, owns a namespaced CAS checkpoint across nine resumable phases, then proves exact convergence and a target version canary. Retained scalar types and dotted keys survive, and explicit context selection pins Helm and kubectl. Same version verification names skipped phases separately, and Helm timeout must cover the rendered drain budget. Caller key replacement rolls API and worker, while connector proxies move on redeploy or enabled reconciliation. An absent or partial caller credential pair refuses before upgrade mutation; upgrade does not generate a missing pair. Cluster up retains installed runner settings, verifies unowned controller reuse and handles rendered RuntimeClass NotFound before install. Cluster teardown bounds owned namespace deletion to 300 seconds, preserves finalizers, and reports remaining phase, conditions, objects and an exact resume command. A remaining owned namespace yields a transient failure unless an independent permanent teardown failure takes precedence. The controller preflight rejects current forbidden-NetworkPolicy logs first. An unchanged controller can pass from complete rollout, a current ready leader held beyond the cache-sync bound, and an observed advancing Lease renewal. Earlier restart history does not override that current stable-leader proof. Other startup paths still require startup logs or successful reconciles and reject current failure signals. The v0.12.2 target admits schema revisions 0076 through 0081. The v0.12.3 target serves schema 0076 through 0093; the v0.12.2 window remains historical. ADR 0209 is partly built: schema-migrate renewal shipped, while the short post-drain hand-off lease, attest renewal, and the drain hold hook remain planned.

steps.title: Resolve and pin the target chart
steps.caption: The released CLI downloads the requested release chart by default or accepts an explicit local path or chart reference. Unsafe versions are refused, references are pinned with --version, and a local chart's declared version must equal the requested target.

steps.title: Acquire namespaced checkpoint ownership
steps.caption: The CLI owns <release>-upgrade-checkpoint in the selected namespace through server observed resourceVersion plus holder and action compare-and-set tests. An active holder refuses a second operation; every completed phase is durable and resumable.

steps.title: Validate all pre-mutation contracts
steps.caption: The driver migrates retained configuration, renders target chart schema metadata, validates the live revision and target version, and refuses pending contract or irreversible migrations unless --forward-only is explicit. For v0.11.2 the release catalog and target API both declare schema 0070 through 0070. Absent or partial caller credential pairs refuse before mutation, including dry run, same version verification, and resume; upgrade does not generate a missing pair. Dev caller defaults retain their separate exit guard. The historical v0.12.1 API and release catalog declare 0076 through 0076. The v0.12.2 candidate declares 0076 through 0081, with source-policy and operation structure checked at application startup.

steps.title: Fence and drain the installation
steps.caption: The pre-upgrade hook writes revision-fenced installation authority and refuses stale or unobserved ownership before the workload roll.

steps.title: Migrate once and apply
steps.caption: The migrate phase is a checkpoint boundary; the chart's pre-upgrade Job owns the one schema migration phase during apply, with api.migrate.forwardOnly merged only after explicit admission.

steps.title: Prove exact convergence
steps.caption: The driver checks target images, observed generations, ready replicas, zero unavailable replicas, hook completion, queue health, and the installed manifest rather than treating Helm success as convergence.

steps.title: Canary and commit observed state
steps.caption: A target version smoke canary must pass. Commit reads the release version back from Helm, records that observed version as known good, persists the final checkpoint, and releases only its own holder authority.

flows.label: Factory issue to pull request
flows.summary: Polling observations or optional signed webhooks admit one durable WorkItem for a labelled issue. An isolated agent executes bounded requests, posts status, can be cancelled or recovered, and ends in one pull request or an issue comment. CI and authorized review may revise that same pull request. Declared verification can stop the run before model startup or delegate to named CI checks that must actually pass. An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries.

steps.title: Verify the issue observation
steps.caption: Outbound polling uses durable cursors under a replica lock; optional webhooks require signature verification. Both paths verify provider identity, installation, repository, sender and label authority before canonical WorkItem admission.

steps.title: Persist the WorkItem
steps.caption: SQL owns one issue identity, execution requests, per item start authority, waiting, cancellation, deadlines and the status comment outbox. The selected base branch remains recorded through execution and publication.

steps.title: Dispatch a durable request
steps.caption: The reconciler enqueues bounded execute, terminate or CI continuation events only from recorded state.

steps.title: Claim and recover
steps.caption: The worker acquires the request, waits for capacity when needed, and reconciles orphaned claims without creating a second item. An execution whose sandbox pod is Unschedulable defers as capacity. Delivery and consumer liveness renewals tolerate transport errors only until the last confirmed send plus TTL minus one heartbeat interval. A refused renewal loses authority immediately. Side-effect markers retry before applying the frame, and terminal settlement remains fenced. Runs and evals share this ownership rule. An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries.

steps.title: Run the factory bundle
steps.caption: The recorded repository checkout and deadline reach the isolated sandbox; the bundle implements and judges the issue. The worker binds fresh publication precheck context to each covered turn, and an unpublished execute turn gets one continuation. The worker supplies execution scoped issue read authority for platform get_issue; the API reads the issue and comments with its App installation token, and the sandbox receives no GitHub credential. Foreground plan and diff reviews are enforced. The workflow must be loaded and the plan approved before repository edits. Blocked verification without explicit CI delegation selects an offline failure session before the model starts; reviewer credit exhaustion ends the turn.

steps.title: Precheck an empty publication
steps.caption: When a covered call proposes no working tree change, the runner asks the scoped API route to compare the title and body with a fresh pull request read. Stale, unavailable, and unchanged proposals return nonhalting refusals with no pending approval. A changed title or body may proceed with the metadata_changed verdict when bound identity and current CI evidence pass.

steps.title: Settle publication
steps.caption: The configured automatic policy and fenced lineage create or revise one pull request, while no pull request ends in one issue comment. Canonical verification observations are required before publication. Failed, missing, or unreadable evidence refuses publication; an unavailable check requires disclosure. A refused factory publication snapshot ends with approval_create_failed and carries the existing redacted, clipped refusal detail into the issue Details line. A sanitized-base mismatch names the first 12 hexadecimal characters of both snapshot and prepared commits; repository mismatch wording and refusal behavior remain unchanged. Publication prose reports CI at pull request creation time and points to the issue status comment for subsequent results. Publication snapshots accumulate the response through EOF under the encoded and decoded size limits. Retryable read faults receive at most three reads within the remaining budget, without rerunning the model. Exhaustion names infrastructure read failure in the issue. Idempotent publication creation and execution settlement writes retry transient API faults within bounded authority; unresolved terminal reports retain heartbeat and sandbox ownership until settlement or the execution deadline. Charged publication reconciliation retries back off from fifteen seconds to five minutes.

steps.title: Observe CI and report status
steps.caption: The factory waits for CI for the configured operator wait under the execution deadline and reports the wait_ci phase itself. Failed Actions receive one rerun on the exact current head before a bounded repair round with redacted job log tails. Operator status cards and final outcomes are updated. Every declared delegated check must be observed and pass; unrelated passing checks are insufficient. Accounting separates implementer and reviewer usage, and a missing report stays unknown. When head checks fail, factory CI reads the current base branch head within the remaining observation budget. Matching failing check names or status contexts are reported as pre-existing and excluded from repair, but required Python or delegated checks failing on that base remain unverified. An unreadable base makes every head failure count as caused. Factory status synchronization owns a versioned SQL lease, releases database sessions before GitHub I/O, and runs separately from dispatch reconciliation. Late matching runtime heartbeats may renew before the execution deadline, with one heartbeat-TTL grace before owner-loss cancellation. Verification replay preserves the first observation for an unchanged command. CI reports unavailable required check names and merge_conflict explicitly instead of waiting for checks GitHub will not start.

flows.label: Declared cron turn
flows.summary: Each worker replica computes due cron slots; SQL admits one slot and the worker enqueues a normal bounded turn. A live interactive session makes the scheduled work wait for idle. An operator can test fire a declared schedule through the same admission path. Manual and scheduled admission hold current source authority; any configured policy or operation history closes the ordinary path. Scheduled and manual histories remain separate and retain terminal reasons. Hook fire succeeds only for the durable ran outcome; failed, blocked, skipped and reclaimed outcomes fail while preserving the record and reason. Open runs remain polled until settlement or a transient timeout naming the same-tier record command. Hook record reads an existing run without waiting or judging its outcome. Schedule reads separate newest scheduled and manual histories. Deploy schema v1.2 always includes cron declarations and advisory warnings from the immutable uploaded bundle; unresolved explicit targets warn after successful deployment.

steps.title: Claim one due slot
steps.caption: A unique hook run row and advisory lock prevent duplicate admissions across replicas. A dedicated source gate supplies a fresh snapshot, and configured policy or history refuses ordinary admission before the slot claim.

steps.title: Enqueue the scheduled prompt
steps.caption: The admitted slot becomes a typed cron turn on the shared runs stream. Task-owned source context must remain live before queue and failure effects.

steps.title: Run through the kernel
steps.caption: The normal consumer owns delivery bounds, session routing and the terminal hook outcome.

adrs.title: Kubernetes Agent Sandbox as the interactive runtime substrate
adrs.summary: Kubernetes is the production runtime substrate; Docker is the parity implementation behind SandboxClient.

adrs.title: Stateless-first sessions; rehydrate on resume; no cross-hibernation cache assumption
adrs.summary: Sessions are stateless-first; a resumed thread rehydrates from externalized history, and prompt-cache warmth is assumed only within one continuous claim.

adrs.title: Langfuse as the single observability + eval backbone
adrs.summary: Self-hosted Langfuse is the single backbone for traces and eval storage, fed by OTLP over HTTP/protobuf through a thin attribute mapping layer.

adrs.title: claude-agent-sdk adapter behind a frozen ACI
adrs.summary: The outer protocol is strong; the in-runner message types and plugin format retain Claude coupling.

adrs.title: Security rails are chart defaults, not hardening backlog
adrs.summary: The Helm chart ships security rails on by default: per-agent ServiceAccounts, default-deny egress NetworkPolicy, scoped secrets, hardened containers, and gVisor RuntimeClass.

adrs.title: Adopt-not-build boundaries; build only five things
adrs.summary: Curie builds only the UI, API, dispatcher, worker and runner glue, CLI, and chart, and adopts license-clean open source for everything else.

adrs.title: Multi-tenancy: one code path, pooled RLS, hard-siloed compute
adrs.summary: Multi-tenancy uses one code path with tenant count 1..N, pooled Postgres with forced row-level security, namespace-per-tenant compute, and per-tenant planes.

adrs.title: Per-agent connector auth
adrs.summary: Connector credentials are named by the bundle and supplied per deployment, giving current MCP servers one service or bot identity rather than a human principal.

adrs.title: Approval gates and human-in-the-loop
adrs.summary: A gated turn persists a durable decision and resumes later through a new event.

adrs.title: A substrate-agnostic worker and a channel-agnostic runner (the thin-shim thesis)
adrs.summary: The worker never learns its substrate and the runner never learns its channel; SandboxClient and a Slack base URL are the two enforcing seams.

adrs.title: Concurrency and delivery: at-least-once streams with an idempotent, side-effect-aware kernel
adrs.summary: Delivery is at-least-once over Valkey Streams consumer groups, made safe by dispatcher dedupe, per-thread locks, a finish-race steer, and no retry after side effects.

adrs.title: A git push is the deploy
adrs.summary: Git flow, immutable bundles, and eval fan-out are built; a red eval does not yet universally enforce promotion.

adrs.title: The credential plane: no broker, prefix-mapped, fail-loud and fail-closed
adrs.summary: A model credential flows from a chart Secret through boot env to the runner with no broker, mapped by key prefix and failing loud and closed.

adrs.title: Swappable jobs around an opinionated core
adrs.summary: One curated default per job; a second implementation teaches the interface instead of a speculative registry.

adrs.title: Tri-language frozen contracts: Pydantic as source of truth, generate the rest, gate on drift
adrs.summary: Pydantic models are the source of truth for frozen contracts; JSON Schema, TypeScript, and Rust are generated derivatives gated on drift in CI.

adrs.title: Freeze the eval-case format: one schema, frozen in place under apps/worker
adrs.summary: The suite-with-graders eval format is canonical and frozen under apps/worker, with a committed schema, drift gate, and a byte-conformant CLI mirror.

adrs.title: Rendering-free channel interface
adrs.summary: Semantic Choice and Confirm still render in Slack and terminal. Discord and email are shipped text surfaces; capability negotiation remains open.

adrs.title: Curie is a harness for coding agents: the CLI's primary user is Claude Code
adrs.summary: The CLI's primary user is a coding agent, so commands emit structured output and semantic exit codes, run non-interactively, and the harness describes itself.

adrs.title: Eval completeness: run the same evals at every tier, grade what actually happened, and promote real traces into cases
adrs.summary: The same eval suite runs at every tier through one grader, grades the whole run, and real traces are promoted into eval cases.

adrs.title: Controller NetworkPolicy RBAC: cluster-scope read, namespace-scope mutate
adrs.summary: The sandbox controller gets cluster-scope read-only NetworkPolicy RBAC and namespace-scope mutate, with an install-time gate on informer sync.

adrs.title: `cluster deploy` reaches the platform API via the UI `/api` proxy
adrs.summary: Without an explicit API URL, cluster deploy discovers and dials the UI /api NodePort proxy instead of self-plumbing a port-forward.

adrs.title: Memory port and first loader
adrs.summary: Scoped state-backed agent memory reaches the runner as a harness-neutral boot preamble.

adrs.title: Extract the storage port now; defer the second (GCS/Azure) adapter
adrs.summary: Blob storage sits behind a structural ObjectStore Protocol with a write-once contract, and no second GCS or Azure adapter is built.

adrs.title: A thin broker port at the non-sacred seams; defer the second broker
adrs.summary: Thin StreamBroker and StreamPublisher Protocols cover the non-sacred stream seams, and no second broker is built ahead of demand.

adrs.title: The sandbox substrate is a resilience-only fallback, not a product swap axis
adrs.summary: The sandbox substrate is an internal resilience and portability seam, not a user-facing choice; Kubernetes and Docker stay maintained, no third substrate.

adrs.title: Conversation-history port and first loader
adrs.summary: A fresh or restarted sandbox rehydrates the same thread from durable transcript state, without SDK-native resume.

adrs.title: Proactive within-episode memory agent
adrs.summary: Drafts an injected within-episode memory agent; automatic generation remains absent.

adrs.title: Explicit named-provider egress, resolved at install
adrs.summary: Provider egress is opened explicitly per named provider and resolved to narrow host CIDRs; ADR-0114 later lets a credential prefix infer the provider.

adrs.title: Scoped, least-privilege sandbox state token
adrs.summary: Each turn gets an HMAC-signed sandbox token scoped to one agent's state namespace, forwarded instead of the raw platform key.

adrs.title: Approval authorizers resolve membership in the API
adrs.summary: The API resolves approver membership itself at click time, failing closed on lookup errors, with four approver sets behind one authorizer.

adrs.title: One-shot post-approval allowance at resume boot
adrs.summary: On resume, the worker injects a single-use, tool-scoped, turn-scoped grant from the durable approval record so the runner allows exactly one approved call.

adrs.title: ACI semver, reader-policy asymmetry, and a wire-lock gate that enforces it
adrs.summary: The ACI version follows its own semver with a change-class table; producers are strict, consumers tolerate unknown fields, and a wire-lock gate enforces it.

adrs.title: Bounded delivery: a delivery cap and a dead-letter graveyard
adrs.summary: A stream entry delivered max_delivery times without success is moved to a dead-letter stream and acked, bounding redelivery.

adrs.title: Every verb is answered at every tier
adrs.summary: Every CLI verb either does the work at a tier or explicitly reports the concept does not exist there, never a fabricated empty result.

adrs.title: LLM-as-a-Verifier grader and progress signal
adrs.summary: The semantic provenance grader is an accepted slot, but no verifier grader exists in Python or Rust today.

adrs.title: Converged approval gates: durable provenance, loud route resolution, and observe-only resume reconciliation
adrs.summary: Both approval paths share one lifecycle: runner-authored gate kind and granted tool are persisted, route resolution fails loud, and resume reconciliation only observes.

adrs.title: ADR-0048: Declare the model endpoint's wire protocol and credential keys
adrs.summary: CURIE_MODEL_API_BACKEND declares the model wire protocol and CURIE_MODEL_ENV_KEY the credential variable; non-Anthropic wires are rejected explicitly.

adrs.title: The boot env is a declared contract: BootEnv, producer ownership, and generated env keys
adrs.summary: The boot env is declared once as BootEnv in aci-protocol, composing SessionConfig, with env keys in the schema so codegen emits every lane's view.

adrs.title: Add an expected terminal status to the frozen eval-case format
adrs.summary: Eval cases gain an optional expect_status of done or awaiting-approval, so a held approval gate can be asserted as a passing result.

adrs.title: Local Docker runner containers are hardened and network-isolated
adrs.summary: Local Docker runner containers run read-only, capability-dropped, without privilege escalation or the Docker socket, on a network with no data tier.

adrs.title: The fake model is a plumbing fixture, not a subject under test
adrs.summary: The fake model is a plumbing fixture: fake-tier eval turns must complete but are never graded, yielding a distinct plumbing_ok outcome.

adrs.title: The sandbox is a bounded resource envelope; capacity is a tenant boundary
adrs.summary: Every sandbox declares bounded resources on every dimension, bundle ingestion is size-bounded, and tenant capacity is enforced by quotas and priority classes.

adrs.title: The harness is a declared package
adrs.summary: Harness assets and selection are declared; only the built-in Claude contribution exists.

adrs.title: Out-of-process harness boundary
adrs.summary: Would make alternate harness adapters consumable out of process across an Omnigent-compatible wire.

adrs.title: Harness conformance has teeth
adrs.summary: A reusable conformance suite exists; third-party production contributions have not yet proved it.

adrs.title: Message-driven approval reply surface
adrs.summary: In zero-Slack mode, local and cluster message keep the CLI Slack stub alive through the approval window and await the resumed reply on the stream.

adrs.title: Versioned JSON Schemas for every agent-facing CLI result
adrs.summary: Every agent-facing CLI JSON result maps to a committed, versioned JSON Schema listed in an inventory that a contract test enforces.

adrs.title: Agent Proxy credential and egress boundary
adrs.summary: Accepts moving credentials and enforceable FQDN egress outside the sandbox; substrate, TLS termination, credential injection, and implementation remain follow-up work.

adrs.title: A closed, versioned attribute schema for the runner's OTel span stream
adrs.summary: The runner's OTel span attributes come from a closed, versioned key registry, so an unlisted key or wrong type is rejected at the producer.

adrs.title: Route message-driven approval cards through the connected Slack transport
adrs.summary: When a dispatcher is connected, message routes approval cards and resumed replies over the worker's real Slack transport instead of the throwaway stub.

adrs.title: Inbound triggers as a new event kind
adrs.summary: API owned HMAC hooks mint typed webhook sourced QueuedTurn records. Bespoke authenticated producers converge at the queue boundary, and declared cron schedules already ship. Deploy wiring for declared generic webhooks remains planned.

adrs.title: Console sessions and CLI-minted login codes
adrs.summary: The console authenticates with a revocable server-side session cookie obtained by exchanging a single-use login code minted by the CLI.

adrs.title: Bundles declare connectors; the platform hosts them
adrs.summary: The bundle declares MCP connectors and Curie derives their hosted runtime, secrets, policy, and MCP configuration; lifecycle portability remains intertwined with Kubernetes.

adrs.title: The API renders connector objects; the CLI applies them
adrs.summary: The API renders a version's connector Kubernetes objects as a pure function, and the CLI applies and prunes them with operator credentials.

adrs.title: Per-user delegated OAuth for MCP
adrs.summary: Defines principal-scoped OAuth, control-plane-owned grants, a token-hiding MCP gateway, and missing-auth pause and resume semantics. The service-key mode remains separate and cannot silently substitute.

adrs.title: A reconciler applies connectors, so agent repos need no CLI
adrs.summary: An in-cluster reconciler applies API-rendered connector objects to match the in-force deployment, keeping the API read-only and the CLI path available.

adrs.title: Git-flow resolves deploy targets, so one repo serves many agents
adrs.summary: Git-flow maps a pushed branch to a deploy.yaml target and its agent, so one repository can serve several agents under the same trust model.

adrs.title: A GitHub App gives the platform its own repository identity
adrs.summary: The platform authenticates to GitHub as a GitHub App with short-lived per-repository installation tokens, falling back to a configured personal access token.

adrs.title: A bundle carries its own sealed connector keys
adrs.summary: Defines the cross-language sealed-box wire and cluster-owned opening key; end-to-end production delivery is not yet fully connected.

adrs.title: Tiered memory lifecycle
adrs.summary: Defines agent and channel memory tiers, lifecycle turns, trust, and bootstrap/update obligations.

adrs.title: Port adapters are deployed services
adrs.summary: First-party Discord and email adapters are deployed services on the shipped HTTP edge. The generic third-party adapter kit remains unbuilt.

adrs.title: Hooks are bundle-declared turns
adrs.summary: Drafts scheduled and webhook turns with authorization, silence, concurrency, and test-fire semantics.

adrs.title: Agents search their own surface through the channel port
adrs.summary: Proposes a spike before committing channel search verbs; intentionally not current behavior.

adrs.title: External native session checkpoints
adrs.summary: Makes provider-native checkpoints an optional harness capability while retaining portable projection.

adrs.title: An approver is an authenticated principal
adrs.summary: Approval resolution derives authenticated chat, Console, or operator principals from credentials; membership, not requester inequality, decides authority, and the platform key alone cannot resolve.

adrs.title: An agent reads its own runs
adrs.summary: Proposes a first-party scoped runs MCP surface with structured attribution and fail-closed identity.

adrs.title: Deploy targets carry environment values
adrs.summary: Moves environment-specific non-secret values onto deploy targets while preserving connector declaration shape.

adrs.title: Retention, capacity, and back pressure are one policy
adrs.summary: Would admit claims against a coherent capacity policy instead of discovering overload after launch.

adrs.title: Deterministic security posture classification
adrs.summary: Computes posture from shipped layers and operator gates instead of trusting a configured label.

adrs.title: Default memory compaction algorithm
adrs.summary: Drafts opt-in, from-source compaction with validation, scope defaults, and an auditable write path.

adrs.title: Bundles declare connector build inputs and tiers deliver pinned images
adrs.summary: Bundles list external MCP servers in .mcp.json and hosted connectors in connectors.yaml, where a build form is built and run as a pinned digest.

adrs.title: Session identity arrives over the ACI so a sandbox can be pre-bound
adrs.summary: The claim path can bind a warm sandbox before the turn by passing session identity over the ACI, without changing isolation rails.

adrs.title: A tool that changes the world reports what it changed
adrs.summary: The action ledger records mutations with conditional SQL completion and undo acquisition. A redacted result keeps neither prior nor post state and cannot promise undo. Restore remains a connector owned verb under accepted ADRs 0121 and 0124, and an acquired undo is not proof its restore ran. ADR 0203 requires approval for undo of a policy-executed remediation.

adrs.title: Binding cardinality is the multi-surface opt-in
adrs.summary: One agent may bind several (kind, address) surfaces. Adding Discord or email does not clone the bot identity.

adrs.title: Durable first-party email state
adrs.summary: The mail adapter keeps ingress and reply ownership in local SQLite with one serialized writer, not in-process maps.

adrs.title: A restore is the connector's own verb, run under the same pinned connector
adrs.summary: The connector-owned restore executor is accepted, with execution under the original pinned connector. The executor is not implemented.

adrs.title: A pending approval's approver set does not follow its route binding
adrs.summary: The allowed approver set is captured when the approval is created and does not track a later binding change.

adrs.title: A snapshot is sealed to the connector that wrote it
adrs.summary: Connector-sealed snapshots are accepted; sealing and the restore executor remain planned.

adrs.title: Managed repository workspaces and approval-gated publication
adrs.summary: The platform clones and publishes through its own GitHub identity. Write credentials do not remain inside the sandbox.

adrs.title: Runtime repository selection is sticky authorized thread state
adrs.summary: The selected repository sticks on the thread as authorized state rather than being re-derived from the prompt.

adrs.title: Deliberate progress is bounded durable channel state
adrs.summary: Progress is durable channel state with a bound, not a substitute for streaming the final answer.

adrs.title: A delivery has one deadline and one renewable fenced owner
adrs.summary: Stream delivery ownership is a renewable fence with one deadline. A second replica cannot steal a live delivery.

adrs.title: A hook shares one thread per partition
adrs.summary: Drafts per-delivery conversation identity for hooks so concurrent firings do not share one thread by default.

adrs.title: A late workspace handoff replaces the sandbox at a fenced turn boundary
adrs.summary: A workspace-capable thread may begin generically, prepare a replacement from durable scoped state, and compare-and-set swap its route only at a turn boundary while retaining prior history and keeping credentials outside the sandbox.

adrs.title: Coding tools are built in and an initial repository URL selects the workspace
adrs.summary: Coding tools and publication are platform session capabilities. An initial allowed repository URL can establish scoped workspace state, while the legacy deployment bit is not the runtime coding gate and late replacement follows ADR 0136.

adrs.title: Curie supports one model harness until a second one exists
adrs.summary: Would retain only the production-read Claude contribution fields and stop speculative multi-harness work until a real second engine can teach the contract; as a Draft it authorizes nothing.

adrs.title: Database compatibility is a release contract; migrations run in one upgrade phase
adrs.summary: Each API image publishes a machine-readable serving window, the target chart is validated before mutation, contract or irreversible migrations require explicit forward-only admission, and one chart phase owns schema migration.

adrs.title: A coding thread owns one fenced pull request lineage
adrs.summary: One scoped server thread and repository own at most one active pull request lineage. Review work starts from the exact verified head, every revision needs fresh approval, and publication compare-and-set advances the same pull request while stale or terminal authority is refused.

adrs.title: The cluster lifecycle admits before it mutates, and its pause authority is installation-scoped
adrs.summary: Records the shipped v0.8.x lifecycle gates: installation and revision scoped quiesce authority, namespace admission before Helm, schema admission before rollback, and clean retry after a never-good install. Draft status records built behavior without accepting the decision. Its quiesce marker is now a short lease renewed while the gate waits, extended only after a clean drain to a roll hold capped at the drain wait.

adrs.title: A channel port turn carries its attachments
adrs.summary: Channel HTTP ingress now accepts opaque attachment references and copies them onto QueuedTurn. The worker selects Slack or generic binding endpoint transport and uses the adapter egress credential for the latter. Discord and mail still emit no references, so their producing half remains unproved.

adrs.title: A channel adapter is a principal, and its credential is scoped to what an adapter does
adrs.summary: A deployed channel adapter receives a bounded adp credential with only channel token rotation, approval listing, and approval resolution scopes for the binding rows it serves. It enters the shared ApprovalPrincipal boundary without presenting the platform key.

adrs.title: Tenant boundary and principal identity land together
adrs.summary: The accepted identity model adds tenant, human principal, provider installation, durable bot identity, shareable agent release, and agent installation concepts in ordered additive stages. None of those schema or enforcement stages is implemented at this pin.

adrs.title: A custom connector is a bundle built HTTP MCP server that holds its own credential
adrs.summary: The draft proposes an authoring contract for bundle-built HTTP MCP servers whose provider credential stays outside the runner sandbox. Historical spike evidence proves the core hosted connector loop, but the draft authorizes no new platform surface.

adrs.title: A long scheduled sweep stays on one sandbox
adrs.summary: A scheduled sweep claims one cron slot and runs through one sandbox on the shared bounded stream.

adrs.title: Signed GitHub issue events admit one WorkItem
adrs.summary: Signed GitHub issue events admit one canonical WorkItem after installation, repository and sender checks.

adrs.title: WorkItems own durable execution identity
adrs.summary: Durable WorkItems and ExecutionRequests own factory execution identity, admission, cancellation and recovery.

adrs.title: The tracker owns dependencies and Curie admits ready work
adrs.summary: The draft would let tracker dependencies gate factory admission; no dependency enforcement is shipped.

adrs.title: Tenant boundary and principal identity land together
adrs.summary: Tenant schema groundwork is present; broader principal and installation boundaries remain unfinished.

adrs.title: Agent and channel memory are written by the agent, guided by editable guidance
adrs.summary: Agents load attributed agent and channel facts and write through bounded memory tools when the operator enables writes.

adrs.title: One installation hosts several bot identities
adrs.summary: The installation hosts several declared Slack identities with routed ingress and reply ownership. Configured and connected socket metrics are independent of process heartbeat, and a relay's optional ReplyHandle.identity selects the named binding while adapter preserves reply delivery.

adrs.title: A mean tester tests an agent the way a person does, from any installation
adrs.summary: The mean tester probes an agent through ordinary surfaces and reports observations.

adrs.title: Conversation transcripts live in their own per-thread table
adrs.summary: Conversation transcripts moved to a capped per thread table with terminal and idle expiry.

adrs.title: A factory run may take three hours and is bounded by time, not turns
adrs.summary: Factory runs use a bounded three hour deadline and explicit turn budget.

adrs.title: The mean tester is one bundle on off-the-shelf MCP servers, and it only reports
adrs.summary: The shipped mean tester uses existing MCP servers and reports observations. ADR 0181 limits every probe to reading or asking, including on test installations.

adrs.title: A bundle may layer its own runner image on the platform's
adrs.summary: Bundle layered runner images are built and selected for deployments with platform base validation. Releases publish the first party factory runner layer, and rendering records layer and platform base digest locks.

adrs.title: Publication prechecks use an execution scoped capability
adrs.summary: Covered factory execute and CI turns carry an optional versioned ACI publication context with a signed ppc capability scoped only to publication.precheck. The runner shares one decision across the stream observer, PreToolUse hook, and can_use_tool, and compares an empty workspace snapshot against a fresh API side pull request read, returning nonhalting refusals without pending approval state. It amends ADR 0143 so this one comparison route accepts the scoped credential. Metadata only publication can revise the bound pull request under current identity and CI evidence, and admission still checks independently.

adrs.title: A bot may limit who can talk to it
adrs.summary: A binding caller list refuses an unapproved speaker before a turn or placeholder is created.

adrs.title: A factory run may test end to end in a namespace it owns on a separate cluster
adrs.summary: Factory test policy permits a named isolated namespace on a separate test cluster.

adrs.title: An approval is answered where it was asked, including by email
adrs.summary: Approval route selection, email card egress and scoped authorization are implemented. Current AgentMail replies cannot establish verifiable sender authentication, so the adapter refuses them before resolving approvals; existing accepted delivery replies remain available.

adrs.title: The connector caller token names the run and work item
adrs.summary: The signed connector caller token can carry paired run and work item identity. The proxy verifies and forwards that identity to scoped tools.

adrs.title: A settled approval card is a record of the decision, and the requester thread reads in order
adrs.summary: Settled cards preserve the decision and requester notices follow thread order. A decision that precedes card registration is settled immediately after registration. Displayed requester identity comes from a validated resume chain and does not alter authorization.

adrs.title: The turn receipt is an install choice
adrs.summary: The installation selects all actions, failed actions, or no receipt in a terminal reply.

adrs.title: Every mean tester probe only reads or asks
adrs.summary: The mean tester example bundle directs probes to read or ask on every installation, including test installations. This bundle policy does not establish that every probe uses per turn read only enforcement.

adrs.title: A signed hook may complete a preposted reply
adrs.summary: A signed hook may request completion of a preposted reply under its authenticated reply context.

adrs.title: Settled stream entries are trimmed; receipts live in Postgres; backlog is counted, not rated
adrs.summary: The worker implements supervised settled-entry trimming. This Draft also proposes Postgres delivery receipts and counted backlog; the observed retention implementation does not establish those remaining parts or authorize the whole proposal.

adrs.title: A factory ticket declares its base branch and keeps it
adrs.summary: Each factory ticket selects a validated base branch and retains it through its work item and publication lifecycle.

adrs.title: The factory polls GitHub for its work, and the platform reads the issue
adrs.summary: Factory polling and optional webhooks share admission authority. Durable cursors and replica locking bound polling, and a platform scoped read supplies issue content without sandbox GitHub credentials.

adrs.title: The sandbox memory credential is scoped to its own channel
adrs.summary: The API confines memory to the current channel, requires a live turn credential for fact writes and records authors server side.

adrs.title: Deployed agents see only their bundle's skills
adrs.summary: The deployed harness exposes only bundle skills while keeping the Skill tool and approval hook.

adrs.title: Automated hook sources cannot widen their tool access
adrs.summary: Accepts mandatory source-scoped read-only authority and fail-closed admission. Durable source policy, operation history and ordinary-path fencing exist, while the complete protected delivery and qualified runtime path remain unestablished. ADR 0203 partially supersedes the premise that an automated source changes no system for prequalified platform execution while preserving the read-only model-turn source-policy invariants; the complete remediation path remains planned.

adrs.title: Protected hooks use a separately authorized delivery lane
adrs.summary: Selects a private protected broker and independently provisioned consumers. Authority records, source fencing, authenticated broker metadata, role ACLs and atomic admission/recovery primitives exist; complete provisioning, worker consumption, artifact qualification and delivery remain planned.

adrs.title: Cluster up reads a missing RuntimeClass before install
adrs.summary: Cluster up reads the rendered RuntimeClass before Helm. NotFound can infer gVisor off before install; Forbidden retains the exact admission retry, and explicit settings or unreadable evidence remain fail closed.

adrs.title: A version-only delta reuses its parent's checks
adrs.summary: The release authorizer may use the nearest fully green first-parent ancestor within ten steps only while its aggregate delta is version-only. Any concluded non-passing required check on the tagged commit still refuses. Reduced PR checks and second-parent proof do not qualify.

adrs.title: Combined preparation PR checks can prove an unchanged release merge
adrs.summary: Proposes accepting the exact full-green combined preparation head only for an up-to-date merge with an empty or version-only merge delta. This Draft is not implemented or release authority; combined preparation still waits for the merge commit checks unless the existing first-parent exception applies.

adrs.title: Automated remediation is a pre-qualified action the platform executes and verifies
adrs.summary: Administrator-bound prequalified platform execution and verification are accepted. Actions outside policy require approval, and undo of a policy-executed remediation is approval-gated. Complete qualified execution and the connector-owned restore executor remain planned.

adrs.title: A factory run lost with its worker is re-admitted as a new attempt
adrs.summary: An owner-lost factory request settles before a new attempt is admitted on the same WorkItem, bounded to three consecutive owner losses. Status cards show RETRYING only when a successor was admitted; other failed and expired requests show NEEDS HUMAN. Acquired but unstarted requests renew their short lease every twenty seconds. Only not_started deferrals count toward the default five-attempt start cap; capacity and thread-busy waits do not. Started factory CI and approval continuations wait for sandbox capacity within their existing delivery and execution deadlines without charging runner retries.

adrs.title: A delivery owner rides through an ownership store outage shorter than its lease
adrs.summary: Delivery and consumer liveness renewals tolerate transport errors only until the last confirmed send plus TTL minus one heartbeat interval. A refused renewal loses authority immediately. Side-effect markers retry before applying the frame, and terminal settlement remains fenced. Runs and evals share this ownership rule.

adrs.title: A factory PR opened after its request was cancelled is adopted by the next run
adrs.summary: Accepted orphaned PR adoption and explicit refusal naming are planned. The current precheck still refuses an absent WorkItem lineage link; this release does not claim adoption is shipped.

adrs.title: Pause authority after a drain is a lease held by a live upgrade step
adrs.summary: Accepted post-drain handoff, renew-only schema migration authority and final roll-hold hook are planned. Current clean drain still writes the long roll hold.

adrs.title: A work item owner rides through a store outage and stops its turn when it cannot
adrs.summary: Would extend the delivery-lease outage ride-through to the SQL runtime heartbeat of started factory requests, and stop the turn when ownership cannot be confirmed.

investments.title: Close remaining channel interaction and the generic adapter kit
investments.why: Slack, Discord, and email prove ingress and HTTP reply, the built-in cluster-message relay proves a third ReplySink, and a scoped adapter principal now carries approval decisions without the platform key. A real second interactive adapter, Choice/Confirm outside Slack, and the generic third-party adapter kit remain unproved or unbuilt.
investments.unlock: Discord or email approvals through the scoped adapter principal, a re-evaluated Communication grade, and a kit only if a third-party channel needs it.

investments.title: Run a genuinely different harness through the ACI
investments.why: The outer contract is strong, but the current in-process path and bundle distribution wedge still hide the real replacement cost.
investments.unlock: Credible Codex/ADK/Strands support, truthful harness conformance, optional native checkpoints.

investments.title: Close the semantic eval and promotion gap
investments.why: The parity ladder is the product promise, but provenance quality and red-eval promotion still have reserved or validated-only clauses.
investments.unlock: Fatal cluster quality gates, meaningful source verification, stronger PR-to-production trust.

investments.title: Close declared webhook deployment gaps
investments.why: Seven bespoke trigger producers and a lost factory label reconciler converge on QueuedTurn rather than a unified trigger port. Cron schedules ship, while declared generic webhook deployment wiring remains absent.
investments.unlock: Bundle declared webhook installation, explicit delivery destinations, and operator admission that preserve each producer's existing authority and bounded queue delivery.

investments.title: Move credentials and enforceable egress out of the sandbox
investments.why: The current service-key path and accepted delegated-OAuth design expose the same unresolved security boundary: credentials, principal binding, and enforceable egress still span several owners.
investments.unlock: Stronger tenant isolation, explicit service versus delegated identity, per-person MCP authority, centralized credential policy, and auditable outbound access.

investments.title: Neutralize the observability read side
investments.why: OTLP is already a good write port; vendor attributes, route names, and read modules are the remaining concentrated leakage.
investments.unlock: A practical second trace backend without UI or API contract churn.

productAltitudes.label: Platform capability
productAltitudes.description: Capabilities that remove an adoption blocker: on premises operation, the channel surfaces, security, identity, and open source model choice. Every component that carries no altitude is read as platform.

productAltitudes.label: Bot capability
productAltitudes.description: Bundles, evals, and operating patterns that ride the isolated runtime. They are reasons to buy rather than architecture peers of the worker or the runner.

productAltitudes.label: Deployed agent
productAltitudes.description: One agent as it exists in an install: an identity, a bundle, and a deployment. An agent may be authored anywhere; Curie gives it an identity and a channel.
